definition_en: the room in a court building where cases are heard and tried
core_image: 一间被木栏切成两半的屋子：法官高坐其上，两方各占一桌，最后一排长椅留给旁听的人
scene: 旁听席坐满，木栏把审判区与人群隔开，法槌落下前全场安静下来。The courtroom fell silent as the judge took her seat.
sceneCN: 这里 courtroom 指法院里专门开庭审案的房间（第 1 个义项：审理案件的实体房间）；句意：法官就座时，法庭内安静下来。图中可辨识物件：法槌、木栏、审判席、旁听长椅。

pos.zh: 法庭；审判室（可数名词，一间间独立的审判用房）

collocations.zh: 法庭速写（庭内禁止拍照时的画像）

senses.title: The room where a case is tried
senses.definition: the room inside a court building in which a judge hears a case
senses.definitionCN: 法院建筑中由法官审理案件的房间
senses.example: The old courtroom was too small for a trial with thirty witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 那间旧法庭太小，容不下有三十名证人的审判。
senses.why: Court supplied the institution and room supplied the space, so the compound names the institution's own room rather than any room used for law.
senses.whyCN: court 提供机构，room 提供空间，所以这个词指的是法院自有的那间屋子，而不是任何被用来办案的房间。

senses.title: The fixed seating layout
senses.titleCN: 法庭里固定的分区布局
senses.definition: the standard arrangement of bench, bar, counsel tables, dock and public seats
senses.definitionCN: 法官席、围栏、律师席、被告席与旁听席的标准排布
senses.example: A raised bench faces the counsel tables across the well of the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 高起的法官席隔着审判区正对两方律师席。
senses.why: Because every courtroom repeats the same plan, the word also calls up that plan: whoever sits higher is judging, whoever sits behind the bar is speaking.
senses.whyCN: 因为每间法庭都重复同一套平面，这个词也就带出了这套安排：坐得高的人审案，围栏内的人发言。

senses.title: The public arena of a trial
senses.definition: the trial as a public event watched by an audience
senses.definitionCN: 作为公开事件、有旁听者在场的审判
senses.example: The whole town turned up to watch the trial in the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇的人都到场旁听这场审判。
senses.why: Courts are open by principle, so the room is also the arena where the public sees justice being done rather than merely hears about it.
senses.whyCN: 法院原则上公开，所以这间屋子也是公众看见正义被执行的现场，而不只是听说的地方。

senses.title: Where evidence is tested
senses.titleCN: 证据当场接受检验的场域
senses.definition: the setting in which testimony and exhibits are examined and challenged
senses.definitionCN: 证词与物证被逐项查问、质疑的场合
senses.example: Her account changed only once it was tested in the courtroom.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说法只在法庭上被检验时才改过一次。
senses.why: A courtroom is defined less by its furniture than by the rule that statements made there must survive cross-examination.
senses.whyCN: 法庭之所以是法庭，不在家具，而在于在此说出的话必须经得住交叉询问。

senses.title: Setting of courtroom drama
senses.definition: used before another noun to label films, series or books set in a trial
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指以庭审为背景的影视或文学作品
senses.example: The studio bought a courtroom drama about a wrongly convicted engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 制片厂买下一部法庭剧，讲的是一名被误判的工程师。
senses.why: The room offers ready-made conflict and ritual, so it became a genre label; the compound now works as a plain adjective of setting.
senses.whyCN: 这间屋子自带冲突与仪式感，于是成了类型标签，复合词也就直接充当表示场景的定语。

senses.title: Room as a sign of authority
senses.definition: the room understood as a symbol of legal authority and order
senses.definitionCN: 被视为法律权威与秩序象征的房间
senses.example: The empty courtroom still carried the weight of the state behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 空着的法庭背后仍压着国家的分量。
senses.why: Robes, the raised bench and the guarded entrance turn ordinary furniture into signs, so the room can stand for the power that fills it.
senses.whyCN: 法袍、高席与把守的入口把普通家具变成符号，于是这间屋子可以代表填满它的权力。

senses.title: A court outside the law
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：法律之外的审判场
senses.definition: used figuratively for any place where public judgment takes place
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指任何发生公开评判的场所
senses.example: Social media has become the courtroom where reputations are lost.
senses.exampleCN: 社交媒体成了名誉被断送的审判场。
senses.why: Once the room stands for judgment itself, any setting that puts someone on trial can borrow the word and keep its adversarial shape.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这间屋子代表「审判」本身，任何把人置于受审位置的场合都能借用这个词，并保留它的对抗形状。

senses.title: One assigned trial room
senses.definition: a countable, numbered room assigned to a particular court or case
senses.definitionCN: 可数、带编号、分配给某法院或某案件的审判用房
senses.example: The parties were told to appear in courtroom four at nine.
senses.exampleCN: 各方被告知九点到第四审判厅出庭。
senses.why: Because a large courthouse holds many such rooms, the word stays countable and often takes a number, as buildings number their halls.
senses.whyCN: 大型法院有许多间这样的屋子，所以这个词保持可数，常带编号，就像建筑给厅室编号一样。

intro.en: Courtroom joins an Old French word for an enclosed royal yard to a native English word for space. The compound is late, but both halves are old.
intro.cn: courtroom 把古法语中表示围起来的王家宅院的词，接到英语本族表示空间的词上。复合词出现得晚，两个成分却很古老。

items.en: Cohors meant a guarded enclosure and also a body of soldiers; it is generally analysed as com- 'together' plus a form related to hortus 'garden', though the make-up of the second element is source uncertain.
items.cn: cohors 指设防的围院，也指一队士兵；一般认为它由 com-「共同」加一个与 hortus「园子」相关的成分构成，但第二个成分的构成方式属来源不确定。

items.en: Old French cort meant the king's residence and the circle of people around him, and it carried both the yard and the assembly into English.
items.cn: 古法语 cort 指国王的居所及围绕他的人，把「院子」与「集会」两层意思一并带进英语。

items.en: By the thirteenth century court in English covered a royal palace, its yard, and the sovereign's court of justice; the legal sense then settled on the body that hears cases.
items.cn: 到十三世纪，英语 court 已兼指王宫、宫院与国王的法庭；法律一义随后固定在审理案件的机构上。

items.en: Room goes back to Old English rum 'space, extent', a native Germanic noun; it named open space before it named a walled chamber.
items.cn: room 上溯古英语 rum「空间、范围」，是日耳曼语本族名词；它先指开阔的空间，后来才指有墙的房间。

items.en: Courtroom is recorded only in the nineteenth century, when court buildings began to set aside rooms used solely for hearings; earlier English said court house or court chamber.
items.cn: courtroom 到十九世纪才有记录，当时法院建筑开始专设只用于开庭的房间；更早的英语说「法院楼」或「法庭厅」。

items.en: The exact first date of the compound is an approximation, since dictionaries differ over which nineteenth-century citation counts as the earliest; the chain of the two parts is clear.
items.cn: 这个复合词的确切首见年代只是约数，各家辞书对哪条十九世纪书证算最早并不一致；两个成分的来源链则是清楚的。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same court element; group two holds spaces that also host legal proceedings but are not trial rooms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 court 这一成分的词；第二组是同样举行法律程序、却不是审判室的空间。

entries.definition: The institution, the yard or the playing surface; courtroom is only its room.
entries.definitionCN: 机构、院子或球场；courtroom 只是它的房间。

entries.definition: The whole building that contains courtrooms; a courthouse may hold several courtrooms.
entries.definitionCN: 容纳法庭的整栋建筑；一栋法院楼可以有多间法庭。

entries.definition: Court plus yard, naming the enclosed open ground rather than a room.
entries.definitionCN: 由 court 加 yard 构成，指围起来的露天场地，而不是房间。

entries.definition: A person at a royal court; the -ier suffix marks people, not places.
entries.definitionCN: 宫廷里的人；-ier 后缀标记人，而不是地方。

entries.definition: A room, often private or official; a judge's chamber is an office, not a trial room.
entries.definitionCN: 房间，常指私用或公务用房；法官的内室是办公室，不是审判室。

entries.definition: The building as a whole, including lobbies, clerk offices and security lines.
entries.definitionCN: 整栋建筑，包括门厅、书记处与安检通道。

entries.definition: A body with power to judge, such as an arbitration or refugee tribunal; it may sit in an ordinary room.
entries.definitionCN: 有权裁判的机构，如仲裁庭或难民法庭；它可能就设在普通房间。

entries.definition: A room for hearings and preliminary matters, usually smaller and without a jury box.
entries.definitionCN: 用于听证与程序性事项的房间，通常更小，也没有陪审席。

entries.definition: The enclosed place where the accused stands inside a courtroom.
entries.definitionCN: 法庭内被告所站的围合位置。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real English halves of the compound and the real building terms around it.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个复合词两个真实的英语成分，以及它周围真实的建筑用语。

normal.en: Court means an enclosed yard and the body that judges; room means a space. The compound is simply the judging body's own space.
normal.cn: court 指围起来的院子，也指审案的机构；room 指空间。复合起来就是审案机构自己的那间屋子。

normal.en: The building is a courthouse, one room inside it is a courtroom, so the pair works like house and room.
normal.cn: 整栋楼叫 courthouse，里面的一间叫 courtroom，二者正好像 house 与 room 的关系。

normal.en: Courtroom drama, courtroom sketch and courtroom testimony all keep the word as a plain label of setting.
normal.cn: 法庭剧、法庭速写、法庭证词都把这个词当作纯粹的场景标签使用。

normal.en: In the courtroom is the fixed phrase for what happens during a hearing, as opposed to in court, which names the case being heard.
normal.cn: 当庭发生的具体场景用「在法庭里」这一固定说法，而「在法院」指的是案件正在审理。

normal.en: The layout is stable enough to be named: bench, bar, well, dock, jury box and public gallery.
normal.cn: 这间屋子的布局稳定到可以逐项命名：法官席、围栏、审判区、被告席、陪审席与旁听席。

abstract.en: Picture a box cut by one rail into two halves: inside the rail words carry legal force, outside it they are only watched.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盒子被一道围栏切成两半：栏内的话有法律效力，栏外的话只是被观看。

abstract.en: Picture a room that is empty all week and then holds the whole weight of a conflict for three days.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子整周空着，然后连着几天装下一场冲突的全部重量。

abstract.en: Picture a raised seat that makes height into authority, so the tallest chair in the room is also the shortest distance to a verdict.
abstract.cn: 想象一把被垫高的椅子把高度变成权威，于是屋里最高的座位也是通往判决最短的距离。

examples.en: Reporters are not allowed to photograph anyone inside the courtroom.
examples.cn: 记者不得在法庭内拍摄任何人。

examples.en: The new wing adds two courtrooms and a secure corridor for defendants.
examples.cn: 新侧翼增加了两间法庭和一条押解被告的封闭通道。

examples.en: Her calm in the courtroom impressed even the opposing lawyer.
examples.cn: 她在法庭上的镇定连对方律师都佩服。

dict_mnemonic.text: court（围起来的院子、审案的机构）+ room（房间）——审案机构围出来的那间屋子 → 法庭

root: 古法语 cort（王宫、宅院）上溯拉丁 cohors（设防围院）；后半 room 来自古英语 rum（空间）。courtroom 为十九世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the physical room to its fixed layout, then to the public trial held in it, and finally to the room as a label, a symbol and a countable numbered hall.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从实体房间走到它的固定布局，再到在其中进行的公开审判，最后落到作为标签、象征与可数编号厅室的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one enclosed room, split by a rail into judging, speaking and watching zones.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间围合的房间，被一道围栏切成审判、发言与旁听三个区。

branches.en: THE BOX AND ITS PLAN: first the room exists, then its unchanging furniture turns space into roles.
branches.cn: 盒子与平面：先有这间屋子，再靠不变的家具把空间分成角色。

branches.en: THE PUBLIC TEST: the same room is where strangers watch and where statements must survive challenge.
branches.cn: 公开的检验：同一间屋子里，陌生人旁观，而陈述必须经得住质疑。

branches.en: THE LABEL: the setting is recognizable enough to name a whole genre.
branches.cn: 标签：这个场景辨识度足够高，可以直接命名一个类型。

branches.en: THE SYMBOL: robes and height make the room stand for authority, and then for judgment anywhere.
branches.cn: 象征：法袍与高度让这间屋子代表权威，进而代表任何地方的审判。

branches.en: THE NUMBERED HALL: a large courthouse holds many such rooms, so the word stays countable.
branches.cn: 编号的厅室：大型法院有许多这样的房间，所以这个词保持可数。

intro.en: Courtroom is a compound of two free English nouns, so it is read by joining rather than by stripping affixes.
intro.cn: courtroom 由两个英语自由名词复合而成，读法是拼接，而不是剥离词缀。

latinIntro.en: Court goes back through Old French to Latin cohors; room is native Germanic and has no Latin source. The two halves therefore have unrelated ancestries.
latinIntro.cn: court 经古法语上溯拉丁 cohors；room 是日耳曼语本族词，没有拉丁来源。两半的祖先并不相干。

items.structure: court (free noun from Old French cort)
items.meaning: an enclosed yard; a judging body
items.meaningCN: 围起来的院子；审案机构
items.example: The court sat for three days.

items.structure: room (free noun from Old English rum)
items.meaning: space; a walled part of a building
items.meaningCN: 空间；建筑中被墙隔出的一部分
items.exampleCN: 这间屋子能容纳四十人。

items.structure: court + room (compound of two free nouns)
items.meaningCN: 审案机构自有的房间（由两个自由名词复合，语义由「院子」收窄到「审判用房」）
容纳法院的整栋建筑（由「院子」扩大到「整栋房屋」）
围起来的露天场地（由「院子」保留露天义）

items.meaning: a person attached to a royal court
items.meaningCN: 依附宫廷的人（加人名词后缀后，由场所转向场所中的人）
items.example: A courtier whispered to the queen.

items.meaning: polished in the manner of a royal court
items.meaningCN: 宫廷式的、彬彬有礼的（形容词后缀使场所变成风格）
items.exampleCN: 他以宫廷式的优雅鞠了一躬。

items.meaningCN: 宽敞的（形容词后缀把空间变成性质）
items.example: The bench is roomy enough for three judges.
items.exampleCN: 这张法官席坐三位法官足够宽敞。

items.meaning: a play or series set in a trial
items.meaningCN: 以庭审为背景的戏剧或剧集（复合后由场所变成作品类型）
items.example: The series is a courtroom drama.

latinEntries.meaning: an enclosed yard; a body of soldiers
garden; the probable second element of cohors
latinEntries.meaningCN: 园子；可能是 cohors 的第二个成分

latinEntries.meaning: a courtyard attached to a house

definition_zh: 诉讼；官司；已向法院提起的民事案件
definition_en: a civil case brought by one party against another in a court of law
core_image: 一叠写满诉求的纸被送进法院的收件窗口，从此两个人的争执变成一件有编号的案件
scene: 两家的供货合同谈崩了，一方把成箱的往来邮件交给律师。The supplier filed a lawsuit over the unpaid invoices.
sceneCN: 这里 lawsuit 指一方就欠款向法院提起的民事案件（第 1 个义项：已进入法院的民事案件）；句意：供货方就未付的货款提起了诉讼。图中可辨识物件：成箱单据、律师公文包、法院收件窗口。

pos.zh: 诉讼；官司（可数名词，一件件独立的案件）

senses.title: A civil case in court
senses.titleCN: 已进入法院的民事案件
senses.definition: a dispute between private parties that has been brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 私人之间已提交法院审理的争议
senses.example: The neighbor filed a lawsuit over the boundary wall.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居就那道界墙提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Law fixes the rule and suit is the following of a case through court, so the compound names a dispute that has been converted into a numbered proceeding.
senses.whyCN: law 定下规则，suit 指按规则一路跟下去，于是这个词指的是一场争执被转成有编号的程序。

senses.title: The act of suing
senses.definition: the step of starting legal proceedings against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人启动法律程序的那一步
senses.example: Filing the lawsuit took longer than the hearing itself.
senses.exampleCN: 提起诉讼花的时间比开庭本身还长。
senses.why: The word names the thing filed as well as the filing, because in law the paper and the act that delivers it are hard to separate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指被递交的那份东西，也指递交这个动作，因为在法律上文书与递交行为很难分开。

senses.title: A claim for money
senses.definition: a suit asking the court to order payment or compensation
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院判令付款或赔偿的诉讼
senses.example: The builder brought a lawsuit for the final payment.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方为尾款提起了一桩诉讼。
senses.why: Most civil suits end in a money figure, so the word often means a demand for damages rather than a demand for an order.
senses.whyCN: 多数民事案件最后都落到一个金额上，所以这个词常指索赔，而不是请求作出某种命令。

senses.title: A suit over reputation
senses.definition: a suit claiming harm to reputation or to a published name
senses.definitionCN: 主张名誉或姓名被损害的诉讼
senses.example: The actor's lawsuit alleged that the article had ruined his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这名演员的诉讼称那篇文章毁了他的名声。
senses.why: Harm that leaves no visible mark still needs a form, and a lawsuit supplies the form: the injury is written down and priced.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的伤害也需要一个形式，诉讼正好提供这个形式：把损害写下来并标出价码。

senses.title: A business dispute taken to court
senses.definition: a suit between companies over contracts, supply or competition
senses.definitionCN: 公司之间因合同、供货或竞争而起的诉讼
senses.example: The two airlines spent four years in a lawsuit over landing slots.
senses.exampleCN: 两家航空公司为起降时段打了四年官司。
senses.why: Where contracts are long and money is large, the threat of a lawsuit becomes a normal instrument of business planning.
senses.whyCN: 合同长、金额大的地方，诉讼威胁就成了商业筹划中的常规工具。

senses.title: A suit brought by many
senses.titleCN: 由许多人共同提起的诉讼
senses.definition: a suit in which a group of people with the same injury sue together
senses.definitionCN: 一群受同一损害的人共同提起的诉讼
senses.example: Thousands of customers joined the lawsuit against the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 数千名顾客加入了针对制造商的那桩诉讼。
senses.why: One small claim is expensive to pursue; joining many small claims into one lawsuit makes the cost bearable, so the word covers group actions.
senses.whyCN: 单笔小额索赔诉讼成本太高，把许多小额请求并成一案才划得来，于是这个词也覆盖群体索赔。

senses.title: A suit as leverage
senses.titleCN: 作为谈判筹码的诉讼威胁
senses.definition: the mention of a possible suit used to pressure a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 以可能打官司来施压、促成和解的用法
senses.example: A quiet mention of a lawsuit was enough to bring them back to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 一句轻描淡写的诉讼威胁就足以把他们拉回谈判桌。
senses.why: Because filing is cheap and public, the word can be used before any paper exists, as a warning rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 因为立案便宜又公开，这个词可以在任何文书存在之前就使用，作为警告而不是描述。

senses.title: The long life of a case
senses.definition: the whole course of a case, from filing through appeal
senses.definitionCN: 从立案到上诉的整个案件过程
senses.example: The lawsuit outlasted two of the lawyers who started it.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩官司比最初接手的两名律师撑得还久。
senses.why: Since a contested case can run for years, the same noun can name not the paper but the entire stretch of time it keeps alive.
senses.whyCN: 有争议的案件能拖很多年，于是同一个名词也可以不指那份文书，而指它维持的整段时间。

intro.en: Lawsuit joins two old English nouns of different ancestry: law from Old Norse, suit from Latin by way of French. The compound itself is early modern.
intro.cn: lawsuit 把两个来源不同的古老英语名词接在一起：law 来自古诺斯语，suit 经法语来自拉丁语。复合词本身出现于近代早期。

items.en: Old Norse lag meant 'something laid down, a layer', and it gave Old English lagu 'law, rule'. The same Germanic root lies behind lay, and the legal sense is 'that which is laid down' for people to follow.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lag 意为「被放下之物、一层」，由此产生古英语 lagu「法律、规则」。同一日耳曼词根也在 lay 之中，法律义就是「为众人放下、须遵守的东西」。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow'. Its past participle secutus and the derived noun *sequita underlie a whole family of following words, including sequence, consequent and suit.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」。其过去分词 secutus 与派生名词 *sequita 支撑了一整族表示「跟随」的词，包括 sequence、consequent 与 suit。

items.en: Old French suite meant a following, a train of attendants, or a set of things in order; English borrowed it in the thirteenth century as suit.
items.cn: 古法语 suite 指跟随、随从队伍或一组有序之物；英语在十三世纪借入，写作 suit。

items.en: By the fourteenth century English suit at law meant the pursuit of a case in court, and the verb sue was formed from it. This is the sense that survives inside lawsuit.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，英语里「依法律追究」的说法已指在法院追究一桩案件，动词「起诉」也由此产生。lawsuit 里保留的正是这一义。

items.en: Lawsuit appears in the seventeenth century, joining law to suit so that the legal reading would be unmistakable; earlier writers said suit or action.
items.cn: lawsuit 于十七世纪出现，把「法律」接到「追究」上，使法律义不再有歧义；更早的作者只说「诉」或「诉讼」。

items.en: The first date usually given for the compound is an approximation drawn from printed citations, and dictionaries differ by a few decades; the sources of both halves are not in doubt.
items.cn: 这个复合词通常给出的首见年代，是从印刷书证推算的约数，各家辞书相差数十年；两半的来源本身并无疑问。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same suit family, including one near homophone; group two holds the everyday names for legal proceedings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 suit 词族的词，其中一个读音极近；第二组是法律程序的日常说法。

entries.definition: The root noun: legal action in older use, and also a set of clothes or a set of cards.
entries.definitionCN: 词根名词：旧用法指诉讼，也指一套衣服或一组同花色的牌。

entries.definition: A set of rooms or a set of musical pieces; it came from the same French word but never took the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一套房间或一组乐曲；来自同一个法语词，却从未发展出法律义。

entries.definition: The verb formed from suit: to bring a case against someone.
entries.definitionCN: 由 suit 形成的动词：对某人提起诉讼。

entries.definition: The rule system itself, not the case; law is Germanic while suit is Latin in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 规则体系本身，不是案件；law 是日耳曼来源，suit 才是拉丁来源。

entries.definition: To plunge into liquid or to pickle; the vowel and the final consonant are close, but the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 浸入液体或腌渍；元音与词尾相近，但这个词毫无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: The general word for a matter before a court; it can be civil or criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 法院受理事项的通称，民事刑事皆可。

entries.definition: The formal British term for civil proceedings, as in bring an action.
entries.definitionCN: 英式正式用语，指民事诉讼程序。

entries.definition: Litigation names the activity or the whole set of proceedings, not one countable case.
entries.definitionCN: 指诉讼活动或一整批程序，不指单件可数的案件。

entries.definition: The demand stated inside a lawsuit; a claim may exist before any suit is filed.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中提出的请求；请求可以在立案之前就存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real halves, the real verb formed from suit, and the real phrases used in practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实成分、由 suit 形成的真实动词，以及实务中真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Law plus suit: the rule plus the following of a case under it.
normal.cn: law 加 suit：规则，加上按规则一路追究一桩案子。

normal.en: Suit, sue and suite share one Latin verb of following; only suit and sue took the legal path.
normal.cn: suit、sue 与 suite 共享同一个表示「跟随」的拉丁动词，只有前两个走了法律这条路。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the stages: file a lawsuit, settle a lawsuit, face a lawsuit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出阶段：提起诉讼、和解结案、面临诉讼。

normal.en: A class-action lawsuit is one suit carrying many claims, which is why one word covers a crowd.
normal.cn: 集体诉讼是一案承载许多请求，所以一个词就能覆盖一群人。

normal.en: Law itself came from Old Norse, not from Latin, so the two halves of this compound are strangers joined late.
normal.cn: law 本身来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，所以这个复合词的两半是晚年才结亲的陌生人。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel being folded into a paper folder and given a number: the moment it gets a number, it becomes a lawsuit.
abstract.cn: 想象一场口角被折进一个纸夹并编上号：它一拿到编号，就成了 lawsuit。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking the same corridor for years, always one behind the other: that is what following a case means.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人多年走在同一条走廊上，永远一个跟着另一个：这就是「追究一桩案子」的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone placed on a scale: the scale is the law, the stone is the claim, and the lawsuit is the act of putting it there.
abstract.cn: 想象一块小石头被放上天平：天平是法律，石头是请求，而 lawsuit 就是把它放上去的那个动作。

examples.en: The city settled the lawsuit before the trial date was set.
examples.cn: 市里在确定开庭日期之前就和解了这桩诉讼。

examples.en: A single lawsuit can force a manufacturer to redesign a product.
examples.cn: 一桩诉讼就能迫使制造商重新设计产品。

examples.en: She kept every receipt in case of a future lawsuit.
examples.cn: 她留好每一张收据，以防日后打官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: law（法律）+ suit（跟随、追究）——按法律一路追究下去的那件事 → 诉讼、官司

root: law 来自古诺斯语 lag（被放下之物），经古英语 lagu 成为「法律」；suit 经古法语 suite 上溯拉丁 sequi（跟随）。lawsuit 为十七世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a case from being filed, through the claim it states and the parties who bring it, to the years it can run and the pressure its mere mention creates.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一桩案件走：从立案，到它写明的请求、提起诉讼的人，再到它可能拖的年份，最后到仅凭提及就能产生的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel folded into a numbered file and carried down a long corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场争执被折进一份编号案卷，沿着长走廊被一路带下去。

branches.en: THE FILE ITSELF: the dispute has become an object with a number, and that object is the lawsuit.
branches.cn: 案卷本身：争执变成一个带编号的东西，这个东西就是诉讼。

branches.en: THE OPENING ACT: the filing is the moment the file begins, so the word also names the doing.
branches.cn: 开启动作：立案是案卷开始的那一刻，所以这个词也指那个动作。

branches.en: WHAT IS ASKED FOR: money or reputation, both get written into the claim.
branches.cn: 请求什么：钱或名誉，都被写进请求里。

branches.en: WHO CARRIES IT: one company or a crowd of customers can be the party that sets the file moving.
branches.cn: 谁在推动：一家公司或一大群顾客都可能成为让案卷往前走的一方。

branches.en: THE FILE AS FORCE: before it exists it can still pressure, and once it exists it can outlast the people who opened it.
branches.cn: 案卷的力量：存在之前就能施压，存在之后又能比立案的人活得更久。

intro.en: Lawsuit is a compound of two free nouns, so its structure is read by joining rather than by adding affixes; only the derived verb and adjective show suffixes.
intro.cn: lawsuit 由两个自由名词复合而成，结构靠拼接来读，而不是靠加词缀；只有派生出的动词与形容词带后缀。

latinIntro.en: Suit goes back to Latin sequi 'to follow', while law is Germanic and unrelated to Latin lex 'law'. The family of sequi also gives sequence, consequent and obsequious.
latinIntro.cn: suit 上溯拉丁 sequi「跟随」；law 是日耳曼语词，与拉丁 lex「法律」并无亲缘。sequi 词族还衍生 sequence、consequent 与 obsequious。

items.structure: law (free noun from Old English lagu, from Old Norse lag)
items.meaning: a rule laid down for a community
items.meaningCN: 为群体放下、须遵守的规则
items.example: The new law takes effect in spring.

items.structure: suit (free noun from Old French suite, from Latin sequi)
items.meaningCN: 跟随；法律诉讼
items.example: He brought a suit against the firm.
items.exampleCN: 他对这家公司提起了诉讼。

items.structure: law + suit (compound of two free nouns)
items.meaning: a civil case brought under the law
items.meaningCN: 依法律提起的民事案件（复合后由「跟随」收窄为「进入法院的案件」）

items.meaning: to bring a case against someone
items.meaningCN: 对某人提起诉讼（由名词逆构出动词，语义由「跟随」变为「启动追究」）

items.meaning: the act of bringing a case
items.meaningCN: 提起诉讼的行为（动名词后缀把动作名词化）
items.example: Suing is cheaper than most people think.
items.exampleCN: 打官司比多数人想的便宜。

items.meaningCN: 法律允许的（形容词后缀把规则变成性质）
无法无天的（否定后缀把「有规则」翻成「无规则」）
items.example: The district grew lawless after the floods.
items.exampleCN: 洪水之后该地区变得无法无天。

items.structure: law + -yer (person suffix, variant of Old French -ier)
items.meaningCN: 以法律为业的人（人名词缀把规则变成一个职业者）

items.structure: suit + case (compound, different sense of suit)
items.meaningCN: 装衣物的旅行箱（这里的 suit 取「一套衣服」义，与诉讼义无关）

latinEntries.meaning: a way followed; a course, a sect

definition_zh: 诉讼；诉讼程序；（总称）打官司
definition_en: the process of taking a dispute to a court and arguing it there, or the cases so handled
core_image: 两个人隔着长桌，把同一件事的两种说法各装进文件盒，盒子越堆越高，走廊越走越长
scene: 两家公司为一项专利争了多年，文件盒在会议室里堆到墙边。Years of litigation drained the budget before any ruling came.
sceneCN: 这里 litigation 指持续多年的诉讼过程（第 2 个义项：官司从立案到裁决的漫长进行）；句意：在裁决到来之前，多年的诉讼已经耗尽了预算。图中可辨识物件：文件盒、长桌、专利证书、堆叠的卷宗。

pos.zh: 诉讼；诉讼程序（通常作不可数名词，指活动或整体；指多批案件时偶用复数）

forms.label: 复数（专业语境偶见，通常不可数）

senses.title: The machinery of suing
senses.definition: the system and steps by which a dispute is brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 把争议提交法院的系统与步骤
senses.example: The contract sends any disagreement straight into litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把任何分歧直接送进诉讼程序。
senses.why: The noun names the activity rather than one case, because it is built from the verb of going to law plus the suffix of action.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由「去打官司」的动词加表动作的后缀构成，所以它指活动本身，而不是某一桩案件。

senses.title: The long running of a case
senses.titleCN: 官司从立案到裁决的漫长进行
senses.definition: the drawn-out course of a contested case through pleadings, hearings and appeal
senses.definitionCN: 有争议案件经答辩、开庭与上诉的漫长过程
senses.example: Years of litigation drained the budget before any ruling came.
senses.exampleCN: 在裁决到来之前，多年的诉讼已经耗尽了预算。
senses.why: Because the word is uncountable, it easily measures duration: litigation can go on, drag on, or finally end.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词不可数，它天然适合计量时间：诉讼可以持续、拖延，也可以终于结束。

senses.title: A field of legal practice
senses.definition: the branch of legal work concerned with contested cases
senses.definitionCN: 法律工作中处理争议案件的那一支
senses.example: She moved from tax advice into commercial litigation.
senses.exampleCN: 她从税务咨询转到了商业诉讼。
senses.why: Once the activity is regular, it becomes a speciality with its own skills, so the word turns into the name of a practice area.
senses.whyCN: 活动一旦常规化，就会形成有专门技能的分支，于是这个词变成了执业领域的名称。

senses.title: The volume of cases
senses.titleCN: 诉讼案件的数量或诉讼潮
senses.definition: the amount of court business generated by disputes in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一段时间内由争议产生的法院案件量
senses.example: Cheap filing fees produced a wave of litigation against landlords.
senses.exampleCN: 低廉的立案费引发了一波针对房东的诉讼。
senses.why: An uncountable activity can still be counted in bulk, as a wave or a flood, which is how the word reports case volume.
senses.whyCN: 不可数的活动仍可按规模来计数，如一波、一股洪流，这个词就是这样报告案件量的。

senses.title: The road not taken: no settlement
senses.definition: the choice to fight a case in court rather than settle it
senses.definitionCN: 选择在法院争到底而不是和解
senses.example: The board chose litigation over a quiet settlement.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会选择诉讼，而不是低调和解。
senses.why: Negotiation ends the dispute privately; litigation moves it into a public forum with a third party deciding, so the two are named as opposites.
senses.whyCN: 谈判私下结束争议；诉讼则把它搬进公开场合，由第三方裁决，所以两者被当作对立的两条路。

senses.title: The bill for fighting
senses.definition: the cost, delay and disruption that contested cases impose
senses.definitionCN: 争议案件带来的费用、拖延与干扰
senses.example: The fear of litigation keeps small clinics from hiring specialists.
senses.exampleCN: 对诉讼的恐惧让小型诊所不敢聘用专科医生。
senses.why: Because the noun names the whole activity, it can stand for its price: lawyers, years and lost attention all fold into one word.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词指整个活动，它也能代表代价：律师费、年份与被耗掉的精力都折进这一个词里。

senses.title: The act of pressing a claim
senses.titleCN: 提起并推进请求的行为
senses.definition: the deliberate act of pursuing a claim through the courts
senses.definitionCN: 有意通过法院追究某项请求的行为
senses.example: Litigation was the only way left to recover the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 提起诉讼是追回押金的唯一办法。
senses.why: The same noun covers the single decision to sue, because the act and the institution share one name.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也覆盖「决定去告」这一步，因为动作与制度共用了一个名字。

senses.title: The institution of contested justice
senses.titleCN: 以对抗方式解决争议的制度
senses.definition: the adversarial system itself, seen as one way among several to resolve disputes
senses.definitionCN: 对抗式解决争议的制度本身，被视为多种方式之一
senses.example: Comparative studies ask why some societies rely on litigation and others on mediation.
senses.exampleCN: 比较研究追问：为何有些社会倚重诉讼，另一些倚重调解。
senses.why: Zoom out far enough and the activity becomes a social institution, which societies may use more or less than mediation and arbitration.
senses.whyCN: 拉远看，这项活动就成了一种社会制度，各社会对它的倚重程度可以高于或低于调解与仲裁。

intro.en: Litigation comes from Latin litigatio, the action noun of litigare 'to go to law'. Litigare itself joins lis 'dispute' to agere 'to drive, do'. The deeper origin of lis is unsettled.
intro.cn: litigation 来自拉丁 litigatio，是 litigare「去打官司」的动作名词；litigare 由 lis「争执」加 agere「驱动、做」构成。lis 更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Lis (genitive litis) meant a dispute, a quarrel or a lawsuit. Its deeper origin is source uncertain: the Indo-European forms sometimes offered for it are reconstructions, and no single etymology is established.
items.cn: lis（属格 litis）指争执、口角或诉讼。其更深来源属来源不确定：有时为它给出的印欧语形式都是重构形式，没有哪一条词源得到确证。

items.en: Agere meant to drive, to set in motion, and also to do or to plead a case. It is the source of act, agent, agenda and exact, and here it supplies the 'carrying on' of a dispute.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、使运动，也指做某事或在庭上陈述。它是 act、agent、agenda、exact 的来源，在这里提供「把争执一路推下去」的意思。

items.en: Lis plus agere produced litigare, 'to dispute, to go to law, to plead'. The verb describes both quarrelling and carrying the quarrel into court.
items.cn: lis 加 agere 构成 litigare，意为「争执、诉诸法院、在庭上陈述」。这个动词既指争吵，也指把争吵带进法院。

items.en: Litigatio, the action noun, named the proceeding itself. English took the stem through French legal usage in the seventeenth century, keeping the abstract, uncountable sense.
items.cn: 动作名词 litigatio 指诉讼程序本身。英语经法语法律用语在十七世纪借入这个词干，保留了抽象、不可数的用法。

items.en: Modern usage splits the field into civil and commercial litigation, and treats litigation as the alternative to settlement, mediation or arbitration; the plural appears only when separate batches of cases are meant.
items.cn: 现代用法把这一领域分为民事诉讼与商业诉讼，并把诉讼视为和解、调解、仲裁之外的另一种选择；只有指多批案件时才用复数。

note.en: Group one holds relatives built on the same lis stem plus two dangerous near-words; group two holds other ways of naming a legal proceeding.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 lis 词干的亲属词，外加两个极易误认的近词；第二组是称呼法律程序的其他说法。

entries.definition: The verb of the same stem: to contest a matter in court, not the activity as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干的动词：在法院争讼，而不是指整项活动。

entries.definition: A party to a case; the -ant suffix marks the one doing, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 案件的一方；-ant 后缀标记做事的人，而不是事情本身。

entries.definition: Fond of suing, or relating to lawsuits; the -ous suffix turns the activity into a trait.
entries.definitionCN: 好打官司的，或与诉讼有关的；-ous 后缀把活动变成一种性情。

entries.definition: Lawmaking, from lex 'law' plus latio 'a bringing'; it is close in sound to litigation but shares no stem.
entries.definitionCN: 立法，由 lex「法律」加 latio「带来」构成；读音与 litigation 相近，却没有共同词干。

entries.definition: A repeated prayer or a long list, from Greek litaneia 'supplication'; the opening letters match but the source does not.
entries.definitionCN: 连祷或一长串清单，来自希腊 litaneia「恳求」；开头字母相同，来源却不同。

entries.definition: A single civil case with a number; litigation is the activity those cases make up.
entries.definitionCN: 有编号的单件民事案件；litigation 是这些案件构成的活动。

entries.definition: The formal steps recorded in a case, or the record of them; more procedural, less combative.
entries.definitionCN: 案件中记录在案的形式步骤或其记录；更偏程序，对抗色彩较淡。

entries.definition: Dispute resolution before a private arbitrator rather than a court; often named as the alternative to litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 由私人仲裁员而非法院解决争议，常被视为诉讼之外的替代方式。

entries.definition: The formal British name for a civil suit; it points to one case rather than to the whole activity.
entries.definitionCN: 英式正式说法，指一件民事诉讼；它指向单件案件，而不是整个活动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin stems, the real word family and the fixed phrases of practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词干、真实的同族词与实务中的固定说法。

normal.en: Lis 'dispute' plus agere 'drive': to drive a dispute forward is to litigate.
normal.cn: lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」：把争执一路推下去，就是打官司。

normal.en: The family runs litigate, litigant, litigator, litigious and relitigate, all on the same stem.
normal.cn: 同族词有 litigate、litigant、litigator、litigious 与 relitigate，全在同一词干上。

normal.en: Legislation looks and sounds close, but it is lex plus latio, lawmaking, not case-fighting.
normal.cn: legislation 形音都近，却由 lex 加 latio 构成，指立法，不是打官司。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: civil litigation, commercial litigation, litigation costs.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出领域：民事诉讼、商业诉讼、诉讼费用。

normal.en: The word is normally uncountable, so it behaves like water: a wave of litigation, years of litigation.
normal.cn: 这个词通常不可数，行为像水：一波诉讼、多年诉讼。

abstract.en: Picture two people pushing the same heavy box from opposite ends down a corridor that has no exit.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从两端推同一只重箱子，走在一条没有出口的走廊上。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that only bills by the year, never by the hour: that is how litigation measures time.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只按年计费、从不按小时计费的钟：诉讼就是这样计量时间的。

abstract.en: Picture a public stage where a private quarrel must be performed in costume before a stranger decides how it ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一个公开舞台，私人的口角必须穿着戏服演一遍，再由陌生人决定它怎么结束。

examples.en: The insurer set aside a fund for litigation over the collapsed bridge.
examples.cn: 保险公司为垮桥一事的诉讼预留了一笔资金。

examples.en: Most disputes never reach litigation because the cost is known in advance.
examples.cn: 多数争议从未进入诉讼，因为费用事先就清楚了。

examples.en: She built a career in environmental litigation.
examples.cn: 她在环境诉讼领域建立了事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立案＋跟踪」——案子立了还要一路跟下去，跟得越久越像一场马拉松 → 诉讼

root: 拉丁 litigare（争执、诉诸法院）= lis（争执）+ agere（驱动、做）；动作名词 litigatio。lis 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the procedure, through its duration, its trade and its volume, to the choice against settlement, its price, the single act of suing and finally the institution itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从程序本身，经它的时长、行业与案件量，走到与和解相对的选择、它的代价、一次起诉的动作，最后落到制度层面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel turned into files, pushed down a corridor that keeps getting longer.
core.cn: 核心意象：争执被变成卷宗，沿一条不断变长的走廊被推下去。

branches.en: THE MACHINERY AND ITS CLOCK: the steps exist, and because they are steps they take years.
branches.cn: 机器与它的时钟：步骤存在，而正因为是步骤，它就要花上几年。

branches.en: THE TRADE: repeated steps become a skill that people practise for a living.
branches.cn: 行业：重复的步骤变成一门可以赖以为生的手艺。

branches.en: SCALE AND CHOICE: cases can arrive in waves, and each dispute is either fought here or settled elsewhere.
branches.cn: 规模与选择：案件可以成波涌来，而每桩争议要么在这里争，要么在别处和解。

branches.en: THE PRICE: the same activity that takes years also takes money, attention and nerve.
branches.cn: 代价：耗掉年份的活动，也耗掉钱、精力与胆量。

branches.en: FROM ONE ACT TO A SYSTEM: one decision to sue is the same shape as a whole society's way of deciding disputes.
branches.cn: 从一个动作到一个制度：一次起诉的决定，与整个社会解决争议的方式是同一个形状。

intro.en: Litigation is built from a Latin noun of dispute, a Latin verb of driving, and an English action suffix, so it can be read stem by stem.
intro.cn: litigation 由拉丁的争执名词、拉丁的驱动动词与英语的动作后缀构成，可以按词干逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin lis gives litigate, litigant, litigator, litigious and relitigate; Latin agere separately gives act, agent, agenda and exact, which is why the two families look unrelated in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lis 衍生 litigate、litigant、litigator、litigious 与 relitigate；拉丁 agere 另自衍生 act、agent、agenda、exact，所以两族在英语里看起来毫不相干。

items.meaning: a dispute, a quarrel, a lawsuit
items.meaningCN: 争执；口角；诉讼
items.example: The stem carries the quarrel itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载争执本身。

items.structure: agere, egi, actum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.meaning: to drive, to do, to plead
items.meaningCN: 驱动；做；在庭上陈述
items.example: The verb supplies the pushing forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「往前推」的意思。

items.meaning: to go to law, to plead a case
items.meaningCN: 诉诸法院；在庭上争讼
items.example: They chose to litigate rather than settle.
items.exampleCN: 他们选择打官司而不是和解。

items.meaning: the activity of contesting cases in court
items.meaningCN: 在法院争讼的活动（动作后缀把动词变成抽象活动）
items.exampleCN: 诉讼可以比发起它的人活得更久。

items.meaning: a lawyer who fights cases in court
items.meaningCN: 在法院打案的律师（施事后缀把活动变成从事者）
items.example: The litigator prepared for a long trial.
items.exampleCN: 这位诉讼律师为一场长审做准备。

items.meaningCN: 案件当事方（分词后缀把活动变成正在其中的人）

items.meaning: given to suing; relating to suits
items.meaningCN: 好打官司的；与诉讼相关的（形容词后缀把活动变成性情）
items.example: A litigious neighbour can exhaust a small firm.
items.exampleCN: 一个好打官司的邻居能把小公司拖垮。

items.meaning: to fight the same issue again
items.meaningCN: 就同一争点再打一次官司（重复前缀把动作加一轮）
items.example: The court refused to relitigate the issue.
items.exampleCN: 法院拒绝再审这一争点。

definition_zh: 提起诉讼；打官司；在法庭上争讼
definition_en: to bring a dispute before a court and argue it there
core_image: 把一场口角装进正式文书，送进法院的大门，然后在庭上逐条争辩
scene: 合同里写明，谈不拢就把争议交给法院，而不是私下和解。Either party may litigate if mediation fails.
sceneCN: 这里 litigate 指把争议提交法院并通过诉讼解决（第 4 个义项：选择诉讼途径而非私下和解）；句意：若调解失败，任何一方都可以提起诉讼。图中可辨识物件：合同、法院大门、调解桌、双方席位。

pos.zh: 提起诉讼；打官司（就某争议诉诸法院）
对（某人或某事）提起诉讼；在庭上争辩（某争点）

senses.title: Take a dispute to court
senses.definition: to settle a disagreement by bringing it before a court
senses.definitionCN: 把分歧提交法院以求解
senses.example: The two families litigated for eleven years over the orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人为那片果园打了十一年官司。
senses.why: The verb is the act version of litigation: what the institution does over years, two parties do when they choose it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 litigation 的动作版：制度用多年做的事，双方一旦选择就这么做。

senses.title: Sue a person or company
senses.titleCN: 对某人或某公司提起诉讼
senses.definition: to bring a case against a particular opponent
senses.definitionCN: 针对特定对手提起案件
senses.example: They litigated the supplier rather than write off the loss.
senses.exampleCN: 他们选择起诉供应商，而不是把损失一笔勾销。
senses.why: Once the dispute has an opponent, the verb takes an object, because the action is aimed at someone rather than at a principle.
senses.whyCN: 争议一旦有了对手，这个动词就带宾语，因为动作指向某个人，而不是某个原则。

senses.title: Argue the points in court
senses.definition: to present and contest arguments before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前陈述并辩驳各项主张
senses.example: Counsel litigated every clause of the lease line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 律师把租约的每一条逐行争辩了一遍。
senses.why: The 'driving' half of the Latin verb shows here: the case is pushed forward argument by argument, not decided in one gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词中「驱动」的那一半在这里显形：案子是一段论一段论地往前推，而不是一个动作就判完。

senses.title: Choose the court over a deal
senses.definition: to pursue a remedy through the courts instead of negotiating
senses.definitionCN: 通过法院寻求救济而不是谈判
senses.example: Either party may litigate if mediation fails.
senses.exampleCN: 若调解失败，任何一方都可以提起诉讼。
senses.why: Mediation asks the parties to agree; litigating hands the decision to a third party, so choosing the verb marks a refusal to compromise.
senses.whyCN: 调解要求双方同意；打官司则把决定交给第三方，所以选用这个动词就等于拒绝妥协。

senses.title: Carry a client's case
senses.definition: to conduct a case on behalf of a client, as a lawyer does
senses.definitionCN: 像律师那样代表当事人进行诉讼
senses.example: She has litigated patent cases for two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 她代理专利案件已有二十年。
senses.why: A profession can take the same verb because its daily work is exactly this act repeated for other people.
senses.whyCN: 一个行业可以采用同一个动词，因为它每天做的事正是替别人重复这个动作。

senses.title: Fight the same issue again
senses.definition: to reopen or repeat a contested issue in court
senses.definitionCN: 在法院重新开启或重复争辩同一争点
senses.example: The losing side tried to litigate the same question twice.
senses.exampleCN: 败诉方试图把同一个问题再打一次。
senses.why: Because courts keep a record, repetition becomes visible as a distinct act, and the language marks it with a prefix.
senses.whyCN: 因为法院留有记录，重复就成了一个可见的独立动作，语言便用前缀把它标出来。

senses.title: Push a cause through the courts
senses.titleCN: 借司法途径推进某项主张
senses.definition: to advance a broader cause by means of court cases
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列案件推进更广泛的主张
senses.example: Advocates litigated until the polluting plant closed.
senses.exampleCN: 倡导者们一路打官司，直到那家污染工厂关闭。
senses.why: A single case is a tool, and a movement can use the verb for years of cases aimed at one social goal.
senses.whyCN: 单件案件是工具，一场运动可以用这个动词概括多年案件，指向同一个社会目标。

senses.title: Quarrel in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, simply to quarrel or dispute
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，泛指争吵、争辩
senses.example: The chronicle says the brothers litigated over the inheritance for a season.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记载，兄弟俩为遗产争了一季。
senses.why: The Latin verb covered quarrelling before it narrowed to court business, and older English keeps that wider shade.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词在收窄为法院事务之前泛指争吵，较早的英语仍保留这层更宽的意思。

intro.en: Litigate comes straight from the past participle of Latin litigare 'to go to law'. The verb is transparent: lis 'dispute' plus agere 'to drive'. The deeper origin of lis is unsettled.
intro.cn: litigate 直接来自拉丁 litigare「诉诸法院」的过去分词。构词一目了然：lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」。lis 更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Lis (genitive litis) meant a quarrel or a lawsuit. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the Indo-European forms occasionally proposed for it are reconstructions rather than established derivations.
items.cn: lis（属格 litis）指口角或诉讼。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的印欧语形式只是重构，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Agere meant to drive or set in motion, and by extension to do, to plead, to carry on. It supplies the forward push in litigate and also stands behind act, agent and agenda.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动、使运动，引申为做、陈述、推进。它在 litigate 中提供向前的推力，也是 act、agent、agenda 的来源。

items.en: Lis plus agere gave litigare, 'to dispute, to plead, to go to law', with the past participle litigatus. The word kept both the quarrel and the courtroom in one meaning.
items.cn: lis 加 agere 构成 litigare「争执、陈述、诉诸法院」，过去分词为 litigatus。这个词把口角与法庭放在同一个意思里。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century through legal writing, when cases were increasingly argued by trained counsel rather than by the parties in person.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪经法律文书借入这个动词，当时案件越来越多由受过训练的律师而非当事人本人辩论。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb for parties and for lawyers, and pairs it with abstract objects such as a claim, an issue or a clause; the old 'quarrel' sense survives only in historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它说当事人，也用它说律师，并可带请求、争点、条款等抽象宾语；古老的「争吵」义只留在历史文本里。

note.en: Group one holds the same lis stem and two near neighbours, one of which even shares the Latin verb of driving; group two holds the everyday synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 lis 的词干亲属，外加两个近邻词，其中一个甚至共享拉丁的「驱动」动词；第二组是日常同义词。

entries.definition: The activity or the whole proceeding; the verb names one act within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动或整套程序；动词则指其中的一个动作。

entries.definition: A party to a case, marked by the -ant suffix of the one acting.
entries.definitionCN: 案件当事方，带 -ant 后缀，表示正在行动的人。

entries.definition: Given to lawsuits; it describes a habit, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 爱打官司的；描述一种习惯，而不是一次动作。

entries.definition: To make less severe, from mitis 'mild' plus agere; it looks like litigate but the first element is not lis.
entries.definitionCN: 减轻、缓和，由 mitis「温和」加 agere 构成；外形像 litigate，第一个成分却不是 lis。

entries.definition: To make laws, from lex 'law' plus latio 'a bringing'; it is about writing rules, not arguing cases.
entries.definitionCN: 立法，由 lex「法律」加 latio「带来」构成；它关乎写规则，不是争案件。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for beginning a civil case; litigate also covers the arguing that follows.
entries.definitionCN: 启动民事案件的日常动词；litigate 还覆盖之后的争辩过程。

entries.definition: To pursue a criminal charge, usually as the state; it belongs to public law, while litigate belongs to private disputes.
entries.definitionCN: 追究刑事指控，通常由国家进行；它属公法，而 litigate 属私人争议。

entries.definition: To dispute or oppose a claim, in court or elsewhere; it says nothing about procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 对某项主张提出异议或反对，可在法院内外；它不涉及程序。

entries.definition: To argue that something is wrong, or the disagreement itself, before any court is involved.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法院介入之前就某事争辩，或指分歧本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real Latin pieces and the real derivative family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实的拉丁成分与真实的派生词族。

normal.en: Lis 'dispute' plus agere 'drive': litigate is driving a quarrel forward.
normal.cn: lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」：litigate 就是把争执往前推。

normal.en: Mitigate shares the driving verb but starts with mitis 'mild', so it means softening, not suing.
normal.cn: mitigate 共享「驱动」这个动词，但开头是 mitis「温和」，所以它指缓和，不是起诉。

normal.en: The family runs litigate, litigation, litigant, litigator and litigious.
normal.cn: 同族词有 litigate、litigation、litigant、litigator、litigious。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the choice: choose to litigate, threaten to litigate, litigate a dispute.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出这个选择：选择打官司、威胁起诉、就争议提起诉讼。

normal.en: Relitigate adds 'again', because courts keep records and repeats are visible.
normal.cn: relitigate 加了「再一次」，因为法院留有记录，重复是看得见的。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel placed on rails and pushed, inch by inch, toward a distant bench.
abstract.cn: 想象一场口角被放上轨道，一寸一寸推向远处的高席。

abstract.en: Picture a door marked settlement on one side and court on the other: the verb is the hand that turns the second handle.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，一边写着和解，一边写着法院：这个动词就是转动第二个门把的那只手。

abstract.en: Picture the same word doing a small job for two people and a large job for a profession: one act, two scales.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词为两个人做一件小事，又为一个行业做一件大事：一个动作，两种尺度。

examples.en: The company decided to litigate rather than accept the penalty.
examples.cn: 公司决定打官司，而不是接受处罚。

examples.en: Only a small share of complaints are ever litigated.
examples.cn: 只有一小部分投诉真正进入了诉讼。

examples.en: They litigated over the ownership of a single wall for six years.
examples.cn: 他们为一堵墙的归属打了六年官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立替门」——立了案，就得替自己一路守到门口 → 打官司

root: 拉丁 litigare（诉诸法院、争讼）= lis（争执）+ agere（驱动）；过去分词 litigatus。lis 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the plain act of going to court, through its target, its pleading, its choice against settlement, its professional use, repetition, wider campaigns and the old quarrel sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「去法院」这一基本动作开始，经它的对象、庭上争辩、与和解相对的选择、职业化使用、重复争讼、更大范围的推进，最后回到古老的「争吵」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel put on rails and pushed toward a bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场口角被放上轨道，推向高席。

branches.en: THE MOVE: taking the dispute to court, and aiming it at a particular opponent.
branches.cn: 这一步：把争议送进法院，并把矛头对准特定对手。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: the push happens clause by clause, in speech before a judge.
branches.cn: 争辩：推力发生在一条条陈述里，在法官面前说出口。

branches.en: THE CHOICE: the same move is a refusal to settle, since a stranger will decide.
branches.cn: 选择：同一个动作意味着拒绝和解，因为将由陌生人裁决。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: repeating the move for clients turns it into a trade.
branches.cn: 职业：替当事人重复这个动作，它就成了一门行业。

branches.en: REPETITION AND WIDTH: the act can repeat, widen into a campaign, or shrink back to a plain quarrel.
branches.cn: 重复与宽窄：这个动作可以重复、扩展成一场运动，也可以缩回单纯的争吵。

intro.en: Litigate is a Latin verb stem with an English-derived family, so it is read as dispute plus driving plus endings.
intro.cn: litigate 是一个拉丁动词词干，带着一批英语派生词，读法是「争执」加「驱动」再加词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin lis supplies the noun of dispute and Latin agere the verb of driving; agere separately yields act, agent, agenda and exact.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lis 提供争执名词，拉丁 agere 提供驱动动词；agere 另自衍生 act、agent、agenda、exact。

items.meaningCN: 争执；口角；诉讼
items.exampleCN: 这个词干命名争执本身。

items.meaningCN: 驱动；做；陈述
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名那股推力。

items.structure: litigare (Latin verb) used unchanged in English
items.meaning: to carry a dispute through court
items.meaningCN: 把争议在法院里推到底（由拉丁动词原形直接进入英语，语义由「争吵」收窄为「诉讼」）
items.exampleCN: 任何一方都可以提起诉讼。

items.meaningCN: 诉讼这项活动（动作后缀把动词名词化）
替当事人打官司的人（施事后缀把动作变成人）

items.meaning: a party engaged in a case
items.meaningCN: 正在案中的一方（分词后缀把动作变成参与者）
爱打官司的（形容词后缀把动作变成倾向）
items.exampleCN: 好讼的文化会抬高成本。

items.meaning: to litigate the same issue once more
items.meaningCN: 就同一争点再打一次（重复前缀在动作上再加一轮）
items.example: The issue was relitigated last year.
items.exampleCN: 这一争点去年又打了一次。

latinEntries.meaning: having disputed, having gone to law
latinEntries.meaningCN: 已争讼的；已诉诸法院的

definition_zh: 诉讼当事人；打官司的一方
definition_en: a person or organization that is a party to a court case
core_image: 长桌两侧各坐一人，中间是记录者的位置，两个人都被同一份案卷写着名字
scene: 庭上两方各坐一桌，中间隔着记录员的座位。Each litigant was given ten minutes to state a claim.
sceneCN: 这里 litigant 指案件中的一方当事人（第 1 个义项：参与诉讼的当事方）；句意：每一方当事人都得到十分钟陈述请求。图中可辨识物件：长桌、席位牌、记录席、案卷。

pos.zh: 诉讼当事人（可数名词，指案件中的一方，原告或被告）

senses.title: A party to a case
senses.definition: a person or body that is one of the parties in a court case
senses.definitionCN: 法院案件中的一方，可以是个人或机构
senses.example: Each litigant was given ten minutes to state a claim.
senses.exampleCN: 每一方当事人都得到十分钟陈述请求。
senses.why: The -ant ending marks the one doing the verb, so a litigant is literally 'the one litigating', viewed as a party rather than as an activity.
senses.whyCN: -ant 词尾标记正在做这个动作的人，所以 litigant 字面上就是「正在打官司的那个人」，看的是当事方而不是活动。

senses.title: The side that brings the claim
senses.definition: the party that starts or presses the claim
senses.definitionCN: 发起或坚持请求的那一方
senses.example: The litigant who files first often sets the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 先立案的一方往往掌握时间表。
senses.why: Both sides are litigants, but the one who moves first shapes the case, so the word often points to the claiming side in context.
senses.whyCN: 双方都是当事人，但先出手的一方决定了案件的形状，所以在语境中这个词常指向提出请求的一方。

senses.title: The side that answers
senses.definition: the party against whom a case is brought and who must answer
senses.definitionCN: 被提起诉讼、必须作答的一方
senses.example: The answering litigant admitted the debt but disputed the interest.
senses.exampleCN: 应诉方承认欠款，但争辩利息部分。
senses.why: The same noun serves the defence because the suffix names participation, not moral position.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也用于应诉方，因为词尾命名的是「参与」，而不是道德位置。

senses.title: One of several parties
senses.definition: one party among several joined in a single case
senses.definitionCN: 合并审理的一案中多方之一
senses.example: Three litigants shared one lawyer and one defence.
senses.exampleCN: 三名当事人共用一名律师与一套抗辩。
senses.why: Cases can join many parties, so the word is used in the plural for each member rather than for the group as a body.
senses.whyCN: 案件可以合并多方，所以这个词用复数指其中的每一个成员，而不是把他们当成一个整体。

senses.title: A member of a group action
senses.definition: a person represented in a group or class action
senses.definitionCN: 在集体诉讼中获代表的人
senses.example: Every litigant in the class receives the same notice.
senses.exampleCN: 集体中的每一位当事人都收到同样的通知。
senses.why: Group actions multiply the party, and the noun keeps its singular meaning for each person inside the class.
senses.whyCN: 群体诉讼把当事人成倍增加，而这个名词对群体中的每个人仍保持单数的意思。

senses.title: The person who appears and argues
senses.definition: a party who takes part in person in the hearings
senses.definitionCN: 亲自参加庭审陈述的当事方
senses.example: The litigant chose to speak without a lawyer.
senses.exampleCN: 这名当事人选择不请律师、自己发言。
senses.why: Participation can be by counsel or in person, and the word covers the person who stands up, not just the name on the file.
senses.whyCN: 参与可以由律师代理，也可以亲自到场；这个词覆盖站起来说话的那个人，而不只是案卷上的名字。

senses.title: The party who bears the result
senses.titleCN: 承担诉讼结果的当事方
senses.definition: the party exposed to costs and to the judgment
senses.definitionCN: 承担费用与判决后果的一方
senses.example: The losing litigant paid both sets of legal costs.
senses.exampleCN: 败诉一方支付了双方的法律费用。
senses.why: A party is defined legally by what it must bear, so the word also names whoever the judgment and the bill will land on.
senses.whyCN: 在法律上，当事方的定义就是它必须承担什么，所以这个词也指判决与账单最终落到的那个主体。

senses.title: Quarreller, in hostile tone
senses.definition: a slightly hostile label for someone who is always contesting matters
senses.definitionCN: 略带敌意地称呼总在争讼的人
senses.example: The report described the villagers as chronic litigants.
senses.exampleCN: 报道把村民描述成一味争讼的人。
senses.why: Because the noun marks the role rather than the rights, it can shade into blame when a writer wants to suggest too much fighting.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词标记的是角色而不是权利，作者想暗示争讼过多时，它就会带上责备的意味。

intro.en: Litigant is the present participle of Latin litigare used as a noun, so it means 'the one disputing'. English took it through French legal usage.
intro.cn: litigant 是拉丁 litigare 的现在分词作名词用，意思是「正在争执的那个人」。英语经法语法律用语借入。

items.en: Lis (genitive litis) meant dispute or lawsuit. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: lis（属格 litis）指争执或诉讼。其更深来源属来源不确定，为它提出的任何印欧语形式都属重构。

items.en: Agere 'to drive, do, plead' supplied the second half; the pair litigare meant to quarrel and to carry the quarrel to court.
items.cn: agere「驱动、做、陈述」提供后半；两者合成的 litigare 既指争吵，也指把争吵带到法院。

items.en: The present participle litigans (genitive litigantis) named the person in the act, which is exactly the function the English noun needs.
items.cn: 现在分词 litigans（属格 litigantis）命名正在做这个动作的人，这正是英语名词所需的功能。

items.en: Anglo-French legal writing used litigant for a party in a suit, and English adopted it in the seventeenth century alongside plaintiff and defendant.
items.cn: 盎格鲁法语法律文书用 litigant 指诉讼中的一方，英语在十七世纪与 plaintiff、defendant 一同采纳了它。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for either side, in the singular for one party and in the plural for the parties of a case, and it appears in rules about unrepresented litigants.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指任何一方，单数指一方，复数指一案各方；关于无代理人当事人的规则中也用它。

note.en: Group one holds relatives on the same stem and two role words often mixed up with it; group two holds the procedural names for the same people.
note.cn: 第一组是同词干的亲属词，以及两个常与它混淆的角色词；第二组是同一批人在程序上的正式称呼。

entries.definition: The act itself; a litigant is the person, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 动作本身；litigant 是人，不是动作。

entries.definition: The whole activity or proceeding, not one participant.
entries.definitionCN: 整个活动或程序，不是某个参与者。

entries.definition: A lawyer who fights cases; a litigant is the client side, not counsel.
entries.definitionCN: 打案的律师；litigant 是当事人一方，不是律师。

entries.definition: Fond of suing, describing a habit rather than a role in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 爱打官司的，描述的是一种习惯，不是案中角色。

entries.definition: A repeated prayer or list, from Greek litaneia; the first letters match but the source differs.
entries.definitionCN: 连祷或长清单，来自希腊 litaneia；开头字母相同，来源不同。

entries.definition: The formal neutral word for a side in a case; litigant adds the flavour of active contest.
entries.definitionCN: 案件一方的中性正式说法；litigant 多了「实际争讼」的色彩。

entries.definition: The side that brings a civil claim, as opposed to the defendant.
entries.definitionCN: 提起民事请求的一方，与被告相对。

entries.definition: The side that must answer a claim, civil or criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 必须对请求作出答辩的一方，民事刑事皆可。

entries.definition: The side making the demand, common in tribunals and benefit claims.
entries.definitionCN: 提出请求的一方，常用于仲裁庭与福利申请。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle ending and the real set of party terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词词尾，以及真实的一套当事方术语。

normal.en: The -ant ending means 'the one doing', so a litigant is the one litigating.
normal.cn: -ant 词尾意为「正在做的人」，所以 litigant 就是正在打官司的那个人。

normal.en: The word covers both sides: whoever is named in the case is a litigant.
normal.cn: 这个词覆盖双方：案卷上被写到的人都是当事人。

normal.en: A litigator is the lawyer; a litigant is the client. One letter of difference, two roles.
normal.cn: litigator 是律师，litigant 是当事人；差一个字母，差一个角色。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the paperwork: an unrepresented litigant, litigants on both sides, a party litigant.
normal.cn: 固定说法显出文书场景：无代理人的当事人、双方当事人、诉讼当事方。

normal.en: The whole family shares one Latin verb: litigate, litigation, litigant, litigator, litigious.
normal.cn: 整族词共享一个拉丁动词：litigate、litigation、litigant、litigator、litigious。

abstract.en: Picture a file with two name labels on the cover, one on each side of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一份案卷封面上贴着两个名字标签，长桌两侧各一个。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs not good and bad but what each side must carry when it ends.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，称的不是善恶，而是结束时每一方必须背负的东西。

abstract.en: Picture two people sharing one umbrella in rain: both are wet, both are parties, neither owns the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人在雨里共撑一把伞：都淋湿了，都是当事方，却都不拥有这场雨。

examples.en: The court ordered both litigants to exchange documents within a week.
examples.cn: 法院命令双方当事人在一周内交换文件。

examples.en: Unrepresented litigants often struggle with procedural rules.
examples.cn: 没有代理人的当事人常常在程序规则上吃亏。

examples.en: Each litigant may bring one expert witness.
examples.cn: 每一方当事人可以带一名专家证人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「立场跟它」——每个人站在自己的立场，跟着案子走到底 → 诉讼当事人

root: 拉丁 litigare（争讼）的现在分词 litigans / litigantis，即「正在争讼的人」；由 lis（争执）+ agere（驱动）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses treat the same role from different angles: party, claiming side, answering side, one among many, class member, person in court, bearer of the result, and finally a hostile label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从不同角度看同一个角色：当事方、提出方、应诉方、多方之一、群体成员、出庭者、承担结果者，最后是带敌意的称呼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a file with a name on each side of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份案卷，长桌两侧各写一个名字。

branches.en: THE ROLE ITSELF: being named as a party is what makes someone a litigant.
branches.cn: 角色本身：被写作当事方，才使一个人成为当事人。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: the same label fits the side that presses and the side that answers.
branches.cn: 两个方向：同一个标签既适合坚持请求的一方，也适合作答的一方。

branches.en: MANY NAMES: joined cases and group actions multiply the role without changing its meaning.
branches.cn: 多个名字：合并审理与群体诉讼让这个角色成倍增加，含义却不变。

branches.en: THE BODY IN COURT: the party can be a file entry or a person standing up to speak.
branches.cn: 庭上的身体：当事人可以是案卷里的一行，也可以是站起来说话的人。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: the role also means who pays and loses, which is why the word can turn hostile.
branches.cn: 重量：这个角色也意味着谁付钱、谁败诉，所以这个词会带上敌意。

intro.en: Litigant is a Latin participle frozen as a noun, so its ending carries the whole grammatical story.
intro.cn: litigant 是把拉丁分词冻结成名词，它的词尾承载了整个语法故事。

latinIntro.en: The stem is lis 'dispute' plus agere 'drive'; the -ant ending is the present participle, marking the person in the act.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 lis「争执」加 agere「驱动」；-ant 词尾是现在分词，标记正在做这个动作的人。

items.meaningCN: 争执；诉讼
驱动；做；陈述
正在做这个动作的人（分词词尾经法语进入英语，把人从事中标记出来）
items.example: An applicant is one who applies.
items.exampleCN: applicant 就是提出申请的人。

items.meaningCN: 正在法院争讼的人（分词名词化，由动作转为角色）
items.exampleCN: 每一方当事人都发了言。

items.meaning: to contest a case in court
items.meaningCN: 在法院争讼（去掉名词词尾，回到动作）
争讼活动（动作后缀把动作再抽象化）
替人打案的律师（施事后缀指职业从事者，与 -ant 的「当事人」区分）
爱争讼的（形容词后缀把角色转成性情）
items.example: A litigious claimant delays the case.
items.exampleCN: 好讼的请求人会拖慢案件。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 正在争讼的；正在诉诸法院的

definition_zh: 受委托替他人处理事务的人；（美国）律师；检察官
definition_en: a person appointed to act for another in legal matters
core_image: 一张摊开的房契放在桌上，签名的人不在场，另一只手替他写下名字、盖章、把文件递进窗口
scene: 老人行动不便，把过户手续全权交给一位熟悉流程的人，自己留在家里等消息。The attorney signed the deed and filed it at the county office.
sceneCN: 这里 attorney 指受委托替他人处理法律事务的人（第 1 个义项：受托代他人行事者）；句意：这位受托人签下房契，并在县办事处完成备案。图中可辨识物件：委托书、房契、印章、文件窗口。

pos.zh: 律师（美国常指有权代理当事人出庭的法律执业者）
受托代理人（依授权书代他人处理财产或事务者）

derivatives.zh: 代理人的职务；代理身份
事实代理人（凭授权书代办事务者）

senses.title: One appointed to act for another
senses.definition: a person given authority to act in another's place
senses.definitionCN: 获得授权、代替他人行事的人
senses.example: In medieval courts an attorney stood in for the lord who could not attend.
senses.exampleCN: 在中世纪法庭上，代理人替无法到场的领主出庭。
senses.why: The word began as a past participle meaning 'appointed', so the role is defined by the appointment rather than by any training.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是意为「被任命的」过去分词，所以角色由任命来定义，而不由任何专业训练来定义。

senses.title: A lawyer who serves clients
senses.definition: a trained legal practitioner who advises and represents clients
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、为当事人提供咨询与代理的法律执业者
senses.example: She hired an attorney to review the contract before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 她在签字前请了一位律师审阅合同。
senses.why: As courts professionalized, the appointment came to require legal training, and the old word for a deputy narrowed into the modern profession.
senses.whyCN: 随着法院专业化，受托开始要求法律训练，这个原本指代理人的旧词便收窄为现代的职业名称。

senses.title: The advocate at the courtroom table
senses.definition: the lawyer who appears and argues for a party in court
senses.definitionCN: 代表一方出庭并辩论的律师
senses.example: The attorney for the defence cross-examined the witness for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师盘问证人长达一小时。
senses.why: Court appearance is the most visible part of the work, so the word often points to the person standing at the table rather than to the whole firm.
senses.whyCN: 出庭是这份工作最可见的部分，所以这个词常指站在席前的那个人，而不是整家事务所。

senses.title: The public prosecutor
senses.definition: the official who brings the state's case against an accused person
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家指控被告的公职律师
senses.example: The attorney filed charges within a day of the arrest.
senses.exampleCN: 逮捕后一天之内，检察官就提起了指控。
senses.why: In American public law the same title covers the prosecutor, because that officer also acts for someone else, namely the public.
senses.whyCN: 在美国公法中，同一个称谓也覆盖检察官，因为这名官员同样替别人行事，只不过替的是公众。

senses.title: The chief law officer
senses.definition: the head of a government's legal department
senses.definitionCN: 政府法律部门的最高长官
senses.example: The attorney general announced a review of the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 总检察长宣布对那桩合并案进行审查。
senses.why: The title marks an office rather than a private client: the holder acts for the government as a body, not for one person.
senses.whyCN: 这个称谓标记的是一个职位，而非私人委托人：任职者替政府这个整体行事，而不是替某一个人。

senses.title: An agent under a private authority
senses.titleCN: 凭授权书办事的代理人
senses.definition: a person who acts under a power of attorney, with or without legal training
senses.definitionCN: 依授权书行事的人，可能受过法律训练，也可能没有
senses.example: Her nephew acted as attorney during the sale of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 卖房期间，她的侄子以受托人身份办事。
senses.why: The oldest sense survives in private paperwork: the authority comes from a signed document, not from a licence to practise.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义保存在私人文书里：权力来自一份签好的文件，而不是来自执业执照。

senses.title: A deputy in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的代理人、代表
senses.definition: a trusted deputy sent to handle business on another's behalf
senses.definitionCN: 受托代表他人处理事务的亲信
senses.example: The abbey sent an attorney to collect the rent from distant tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 修道院派了一名代理人去收远方佃户的租。
senses.why: Before professional courts, any trusted deputy could be appointed, and the word covered that wide range of errands.
senses.whyCN: 在专业化法院出现之前，任何受信任的副手都可被任命，这个词覆盖了那类范围很广的差事。

senses.title: The in-house legal adviser
senses.definition: the lawyer employed inside a company or institution
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于公司或机构内部的律师
senses.example: The company's attorney flagged the export clause before the shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 发货前，公司的法务律师标出了出口条款的风险。
senses.why: Inside an institution the word marks a desk rather than a courtroom, showing how far the role has moved from public advocacy.
senses.whyCN: 在机构内部，这个词标记的是一张办公桌而不是法庭席位，说明这个角色已离公开辩护有多远。

intro.en: Attorney reaches English through Old French atorne, the past participle of atorner 'to appoint'. The verb joins a- from Latin ad- with torner 'to turn', which goes back to Latin tornare and Greek tornos 'lathe'. The sense 'one appointed to act for another' is older than the sense 'lawyer'.
intro.cn: attorney 经古法语 atorné 进入英语，那是 atorner「任命」的过去分词。这个动词由源自拉丁 ad- 的 a- 与 torner「转」构成，后者上溯拉丁 tornare 与希腊 tornos「车床」。「受托代他人行事」这一含义比「律师」更古老。

items.en: Tornos named a lathe, the tool that turns a piece of wood or metal against a cutting edge. The word survives in English only through the Latin branch.
items.cn: tornos 指车床，即让木料或金属旋转着接受切削的工具。这个词只通过拉丁一支进入英语。

items.en: Tornare meant to turn, and especially to turn on a lathe. The physical image of turning a material into shape sits behind the French verb of arranging.
items.cn: tornare 意为转动，尤指在车床上旋削。把材料旋成形状这一具体意象，正是法语「安排」动词的底子。

items.en: Atorner meant to arrange, to turn to a purpose, to appoint. The prefix a- goes back to Latin ad- 'to', so the verb pictures turning something toward a use.
items.cn: atorner 意为安排、把某物转向某个用途、任命。前缀 a- 上溯拉丁 ad-「向」，所以这个动词描绘的是把某物转向一个用途。

items.en: The past participle atorne meant 'appointed', and it could stand as a noun for the person appointed. This is the exact grammatical shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 过去分词 atorné 意为「被任命的」，并可作名词指被任命的人。英语借入的正是这个语法形态。

items.en: English took the word in the thirteenth century, first for any appointed deputy in legal business, a range wider than licensed lawyers.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪借入这个词，最初指法律事务中任何受任命的代理人，范围比持照律师宽。

items.en: The professional sense narrowed during the nineteenth century, while the older idea of appointment survives in the fixed phrase power of attorney and in the title attorney general.
items.cn: 职业义在十九世纪收窄，而更古老的「任命」观念保存在「授权书」这一固定说法与「总检察长」这一头衔里。

note.en: Group one separates true relatives on the turning verb from words that merely look similar; group two separates the professional titles that overlap in daily use.
note.cn: 第一组把真正同出「转」这个动词的亲属词，与只是外形相似的词分开；第二组区分日常使用中彼此重叠的职业称谓。

entries.definition: An agent appointed by a private document; the base word alone can also mean a licensed lawyer.
entries.definitionCN: 凭私人文件任命的代理人；单用基础词也可指持照律师。

entries.definition: To transfer allegiance to a new lord. It keeps the old sense of turning toward a new master.
entries.definitionCN: 向新领主表示效忠；保留「转向新主人」的古老含义。

entries.tag: shares the turning verb, different sense
entries.definition: From Old French torneiement, a contest of turning horses; it shares tornare but has nothing to do with law.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 torneiement，指骑手拨转马匹的竞技；它共享「转」这个拉丁动词，却与法律无关。

entries.definition: Built from at + one + -ment, meaning 'being at one'. It resembles at- plus torner but comes from a different source.
entries.definitionCN: 意思是「合而为一」；它外形像那个「任命」动词的派生词，来源却完全不同。

entries.definition: The office or position of an attorney, not the person holding it.
entries.definitionCN: 指代理人的职位或身份，而不是担任者本人。

entries.definition: The neutral everyday word for a legal practitioner; attorney is the American formal and courtroom term.
entries.definitionCN: 法律执业者的中性日常说法；attorney 是美国更正式、更带法庭色彩的说法。

entries.definition: A legal adviser or the advocates in a case, often used as a mass noun; it stresses advice rather than appointment.
entries.definitionCN: 法律顾问或案中的辩护人，常作不可数名词；它强调的是咨询而非任命。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer who advises clients and prepares documents rather than arguing in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指为客户提供咨询、准备文书而不在高等法院辩论的律师。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer specially entitled to plead in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指特别有权在高等法院出庭辩论的律师。

entries.definition: Anyone authorised to act for another; attorney adds the legal and documentary setting.
entries.definitionCN: 任何获授权代他人行事者；attorney 多了法律与文书的场景。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real French pieces, the real turning verb and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的法语构件、真实的「转」动词，以及真实的词族。

normal.en: Atorner meant to appoint: an attorney is someone appointed, not merely someone learned.
normal.cn: atorner 意为任命：attorney 是被任命的人，而不只是有学问的人。

normal.en: The turning verb behind the word also turns up in tournament, where horses turn.
normal.cn: 这个词背后的「转」动词也出现在 tournament 里，那里转的是马。

normal.en: Atonement is a look-alike built from at one, not from the appointing verb.
normal.cn: atonement 是形近词，意思是「合而为一」，与「任命」动词无关。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the roles: power of attorney for private authority, attorney at law for the licensed profession.
normal.cn: 固定说法把角色分开：「授权书」指私人授权，「执业律师」指持照执业。

normal.en: The family runs attorney, attorneyship, attorney-in-fact and attorney-at-law.
normal.cn: 同族词有 attorney、attorneyship、attorney-in-fact、attorney-at-law。

abstract.en: Picture a signature line on a deed: the hand that writes it belongs to someone else.
abstract.cn: 想象房契上的一条签名线：落笔的那只手属于另一个人。

abstract.en: Picture a door with two keys, one given by a client and one issued by a court.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门配着两把钥匙，一把由当事人给出，一把由法院颁发。

abstract.en: Picture a title whose meaning slides from 'deputy' to 'lawyer' as the room fills with trained people.
abstract.cn: 想象一个称谓的含义从「代理人」滑向「律师」，因为房间里坐满了受过训练的人。

examples.en: The attorney reviewed the lease before the family signed it.
examples.cn: 律师在全家签字前审阅了租约。

examples.en: In this state a prosecuting attorney must stand for election.
examples.cn: 在这个州，公诉律师必须参加选举。

examples.en: Her aunt held power of attorney during the hospital stay.
examples.cn: 她住院期间，姑妈持有授权书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「托你」——把事情托付给你去办，受托的那个人就是 attorney → 受托代理人、律师

root: 古法语 atorner（任命、安排）的过去分词 atorné「被任命的」；a- 源自拉丁 ad-「向」，torner 源自拉丁 tornare（转）与希腊 tornos（车床）。核心义为「受托代他人行事」，后收窄为「律师」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the appointed deputy, through the licensed lawyer and the courtroom advocate, to the public prosecutor, the chief law officer, private authority under a signed document, the old deputy, and the in-house adviser.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从受托的代理人开始，经持照律师与出庭辩护者，到检察官、总检察长、凭签署文件获得的私人授权、旧时的代表，最后到企业内部的法务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature written by one hand on another person's deed.
core.cn: 核心意象：别人的房契上，由另一只手写下的名字。

branches.en: THE APPOINTMENT: the oldest sense is simply the person appointed to stand in for another.
branches.cn: 任命本身：最古老的含义就是被任命、代替他人出面的人。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: training replaces the bare appointment, producing the modern lawyer.
branches.cn: 职业化：训练取代了单纯的任命，于是有了现代意义上的律师。

branches.en: THE COURTROOM: the visible slice of the job, the advocate at the table.
branches.cn: 法庭：这份工作最可见的一角，即席前辩论的人。

branches.en: THE STATE: the same title covers prosecutors and the chief law officer, who act for the public.
branches.cn: 国家一侧：同一称谓覆盖检察官与总检察长，他们替公众行事。

branches.en: DOCUMENT AND DESK: private authority under a deed, the medieval deputy, and the in-house adviser all keep the core of acting for another.
branches.cn: 文书与办公桌：凭契据获得的私人授权、中世纪的代理人、企业内的法务，都保留着「替他人行事」的内核。

intro.en: Attorney is an Old French participle that became an English noun, so its parts tell the story of appointment rather than of law.
intro.cn: attorney 是一个变成英语名词的古法语分词，所以它的构件讲的是「任命」的故事，而不是法律的故事。

latinIntro.en: The deeper pieces are Latin ad- 'to' and tornare 'to turn', the second from Greek tornos 'lathe'; the legal meaning was assembled in French.
latinIntro.cn: 更深的构件是拉丁 ad-「向」与 tornare「转」，后者来自希腊 tornos「车床」；法律含义是在法语中组装出来的。

definition_en: a person who practises law, advising clients or pleading cases
core_image: 一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗堆在办公桌上，桌边的人正把其中一条条款圈出来给来访者看
scene: 当事人带着一份读不懂的租约走进办公室，想知道哪几条会让自己吃亏。The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.

pos.zh: 律师（泛指以法律为业者，可提供咨询或代理诉讼）

senses.title: A person who practises law
senses.definition: someone whose profession is law, whether advising or representing
senses.definitionCN: 以法律为职业的人，提供咨询或代理皆可
senses.example: The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.
senses.exampleCN: 律师标出了三条可能让租客多花钱的条款。
senses.why: The word is built from law plus an agent ending, so it names the profession by its subject matter rather than by a court role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「法律」加施事后缀构成，所以它按业务内容命名职业，而不是按法庭角色命名。

senses.title: An adviser working outside court
senses.definition: a legal adviser whose work is done in an office rather than in court
senses.definitionCN: 主要在办公室而非法庭上工作的法律顾问
senses.example: Our lawyer reviewed the insurance policy line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的律师逐行审阅了保险条款。
senses.why: Most legal work is paperwork and advice, so the everyday word usually points to the desk rather than to the dock.
senses.whyCN: 多数法律工作是文书与咨询，所以这个日常词通常指向办公桌，而不是法庭上的席位。

senses.title: An advocate who speaks in court
senses.definition: a legal practitioner who argues a case before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前为案件辩论的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer spoke for forty minutes without looking at her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师讲了四十分钟，全程没看笔记。
senses.why: The same noun serves the courtroom because advocacy is the part of the profession the public sees and remembers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也用于法庭，因为辩护是公众看得见、记得住的那部分工作。

senses.title: The profession as a group
senses.definition: lawyers considered collectively, often in commentary or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的律师，常用于评论或批评
senses.example: The lawyers for both sides met privately before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，双方的律师私下见了面。
senses.why: A countable noun used in the plural can stand for a whole trade, which is why the word appears in sentences about the profession as a force.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用复数时可以代表整个行业，所以这个词会出现在把律师界当作一股力量的句子里。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a practitioner who works in a particular field of law
senses.definitionCN: 在某一法律领域执业的律师
senses.example: They consulted a patent lawyer before filing the design.
senses.exampleCN: 申请外观设计前，他们咨询了专利律师。
senses.why: Modern law divides into fields, and the word attaches to the field as a modifier, turning the general noun into a specialism.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律分成许多领域，这个词作为修饰成分附着在领域上，就把通称变成了专业分工。

senses.title: The person who drafts the papers
senses.definition: the practitioner who prepares contracts, deeds and other documents
senses.definitionCN: 准备合同、契据等文书的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer drafted the deed so that either heir could sell.
senses.exampleCN: 律师起草的契据让两位继承人都能出售。
senses.why: Drafting is invisible in court but decisive in outcome, so the word also covers the quiet work behind a signature.
senses.whyCN: 起草在法庭上看不见，却决定结果，所以这个词也覆盖签名背后那份安静的工作。

senses.title: A sea lawyer
senses.titleCN: 好抬杠的水手；爱抠规则的人
senses.definition: an argumentative sailor, or anyone who quibbles about rules without authority
senses.definitionCN: 爱争辩的水手，或任何没有职权却抠规则字眼的人
senses.example: The cook was a sea lawyer who could quote every regulation but never follow one.
senses.exampleCN: 那个厨子是个爱抬杠的水手，条条规则都能背，却一条也不照做。
senses.why: Sailors with time on their hands argued about regulations, and the fixed phrase transferred that habit to land as a mild insult.
senses.whyCN: 水手闲来无事就争论规章，这个固定说法把这种习气带上岸，成了轻度的讥称。

senses.title: A clever arguer on technicalities
senses.definition: a person who argues by exploiting fine points rather than by merit
senses.definitionCN: 靠抠细枝末节而非讲道理取胜的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a lawyer to win that argument, only patient.
senses.exampleCN: 赢那场争论不必是律师，只需要有耐心。
senses.why: Because the trade is associated with precise wording, the noun can describe anyone who fights with clauses instead of facts.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个行业与精确措辞联系在一起，这个名词便能描述任何用条款而非事实来争论的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is an English compound of law and an agent ending. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', while the ending is a variant of -ier from Old French, ultimately Latin -arius.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语用 law 加施事后缀构成的复合词。law 来自古诺斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，词尾则是古法语 -ier 的变体，最终上溯拉丁 -arius。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down, a layer or a fixed order; its plural log named customary law in the Norse-speaking world.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下的东西、一层或既定秩序；其复数 lǫg 在诺斯语世界指习惯法。

items.en: English borrowed lagu for law, covering both the body of rules and the custom of a district, a word that displaced the older native term.
items.cn: 英语借入 lagu 表示法律，既指整套规则，也指一地的习惯，并取代了更早的本族词。

items.en: The Latin agent suffix -arius, through Old French -ier, formed words for people concerned with a thing, and it is the source of the ending here.
items.cn: 拉丁施事后缀 -arius 经古法语 -ier，构成「与某物打交道的人」，这里这个词尾正源于此。

items.en: Middle English had lawier beside lawyer; the spelling with y won out, and the word settled on the profession as a whole.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lawier 与 lawyer 并存，带 y 的拼法最终胜出，这个词也固定指整个职业。

items.en: Modern English uses lawyer as the neutral everyday term, while attorney carries American formality and counsel carries courtroom colour.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lawyer 当作中性日常说法，attorney 带美国式的正式感，counsel 则带法庭色彩。

note.en: Group one separates the base word and the derived family from two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the plain word against the formal and regional titles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词与派生词族，同两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把日常通称与正式称谓、地区称谓作对照。

entries.definition: The rules themselves; lawyer is the person whose trade is those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身；lawyer 是以这些规则为业的人。

entries.definition: Resembling a lawyer or the manner of legal argument, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 像律师的、像法律辩论腔调的，不是指人。

entries.definition: The practice or craft of being a lawyer, viewed as work rather than as a role.
entries.definitionCN: 指律师的实务与手艺，看作工作而非角色。

entries.definition: One who saws wood, from saw plus the same agent ending; the shape matches but the base is a tool, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 锯木的人，由 saw 加同一个施事后缀构成；外形相似，基础词却是工具而非法律。

entries.definition: A law-enforcement officer, built from law plus man; it names an officer, not a legal adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 执法官员，由 law 加 man 构成；它指警官，不是法律顾问。

entries.definition: The formal American word for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: A legal adviser or the advocates in a case, often a mass noun with a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 法律顾问或案中的辩护人，常作不可数名词，语气正式。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer who advises and prepares documents rather than pleading in higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指提供咨询、准备文书而不在高等法院辩论的律师。

entries.definition: In Britain, a lawyer specially qualified to plead in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指有资格在高等法院出庭辩论的律师。

entries.definition: A person who pleads for another, in law or in a cause; the word stresses speaking for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人或某项事业辩护的人；这个词强调替人发声。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Norse source of law and the real agent ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 law 真实的诺斯语来源，以及真实的施事后缀。

normal.en: Law is 'what is laid down', and a lawyer is the person who works with what is laid down.
normal.cn: law 是「被放下的东西」，lawyer 就是与这些既定规则打交道的人。

normal.en: The -yer ending is a spelling of the agent ending that also built sawyer, a woodcutter.
normal.cn: -yer 是施事后缀的一种拼法，它也构成了 sawyer，即锯木人。

normal.en: Sawyer looks like lawyer but starts from a tool, so the two words share an ending and nothing else.
normal.cn: sawyer 形似 lawyer，却从工具起头，两词只共享词尾，别无其他。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the settings: a practising lawyer, a defence lawyer, a company lawyer.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：执业律师、辩护律师、公司法务。

normal.en: The plain word sits between attorney and counsel: less formal than one, less courtroom-bound than the other.
normal.cn: 这个通称夹在 attorney 与 counsel 之间：比前者随意，比后者少些法庭气。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of folders with coloured tabs, one tab for each field of law.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗，每个法律领域一个标签。

abstract.en: Picture a person reading a contract with a red pen, circling what could cost money.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人拿着红笔读合同，圈出可能花钱的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a trade that exists because rules are written down and someone must read them closely.
abstract.cn: 想象一门行业的存在理由：规则被写下来，总得有人仔细去读。

examples.en: A good lawyer tells you what not to sign, not only what to sign.
examples.cn: 好律师会告诉你什么别签，而不只是什么该签。

examples.en: The company keeps two lawyers in house and hires outside counsel for big cases.
examples.cn: 公司内部留了两名律师，大案子再请外部顾问。

examples.en: He joked that every family needs a doctor, a lawyer and a locksmith.
examples.cn: 他开玩笑说，每个家庭都需要一个医生、一个律师和一个锁匠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老爷」——旧时替人写状纸、讲规矩的师爷，如今叫 lawyer → 律师

root: 英语 law（法律，源自古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」）加施事后缀 -yer（古法语 -ier 的变体，上溯拉丁 -arius）。
