sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the profession as a whole, through office advice, courtroom advocacy, the trade seen as a group, specialist practice and document drafting, to the sea lawyer and the mere quibbler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整个职业开始，经办公室咨询、出庭辩护、作为群体的律师界、专长执业与文书起草，最后到「好抬杠的水手」和只会钻字眼的争辩者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tabbed files on a desk, one clause circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上一摞贴标签的卷宗，其中一条被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE TRADE: the agent ending turns the rules into a person whose work they are.
branches.cn: 职业：施事后缀把「规则」变成以此为业的人。

branches.en: THE DESK: most of the work is reading, warning and drafting outside court.
branches.cn: 办公桌：多数工作是在法庭之外阅读、提醒与起草。

branches.en: THE VOICE AND THE BODY: the same noun covers the speaker in court and the profession as a collective force.
branches.cn: 声音与群体：同一个名词既指庭上发言者，也指作为一股力量的整个行业。

branches.en: THE NARROWING: fields and paperwork split the general word into specialisms and quiet desk work.
branches.cn: 细分：领域与文书把这个通称分成专业分工与安静的案头工作。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the trade's prestige also produces mock titles for quibblers and technical arguers.
branches.cn: 讥称：这个行业的声望也造出了挖苦人的称号，指爱抬杠与钻字眼的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is a home-built English compound: a Norse-derived noun plus a French-derived agent ending.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语本土拼装的复合词：一个源自诺斯语的名词，加一个源自法语的施事后缀。

latinIntro.en: The ending is Latin -arius, which reached English through Old French -ier; the noun law itself is not Latin but Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾是拉丁 -arius，经古法语 -ier 进入英语；而名词 law 本身并非拉丁语，而是诺斯语。

items.meaningCN: 被放下之物；既定秩序
items.example: The Norse noun named what was laid down.
items.exampleCN: 这个诺斯语名词命名被放下的东西。

items.meaningCN: 法律；习惯法
items.example: Lagu covered both statute and custom.
items.exampleCN: lagu 既指成文规则，也指习惯。

items.meaningCN: 与……打交道的人（施事后缀）
items.example: The suffix built words for trades.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示行业的词。

items.meaningCN: 从事……的人（经法语转写的施事词尾）
items.example: French kept the Latin suffix in a shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个拉丁后缀保留成更短的形式。

items.meaningCN: 施事词尾（英语中的另一种拼法）
items.example: Lawyer and sawyer share this spelling.
items.exampleCN: lawyer 与 sawyer 共享这一拼法。

items.meaningCN: 以法律为业的人（基础词加施事后缀，指职业而非一次动作）
items.exampleCN: 一位律师读了这份租约。

items.meaning: in the manner of a lawyer
items.meaningCN: 像律师的（形容词后缀把职业转成风格）
items.example: He answered in a lawyerly way.
items.exampleCN: 他用律师式的措辞回答。

items.meaningCN: 律师实务（动名词后缀把角色转成活动）
items.exampleCN: 扎实的律师实务避免了损失。

definition_zh: 忠告；建议；商议；法律顾问；（案中的）辩护律师；劝告
definition_en: advice given to someone, or the person who gives legal advice
core_image: 壁炉边两把椅子相对，一个人把利弊一条条摆出来，另一个人只听不答，手里捏着一封没送出的信
scene: 开庭前一夜，年轻律师敲开老同行的门，把心里的犹豫和盘托出。The junior barrister sought counsel from a senior colleague before the hearing.
sceneCN: 这里 counsel 指从他人处得到的专业建议（第 1 个义项：给出的忠告与指导）；句意：开庭前，这位年轻律师向资深同行求教。图中可辨识物件：壁炉、两把椅子、未寄出的信、茶杯。

pos.zh: 忠告；建议（不可数名词）
法律顾问；（案中的）辩护律师
劝告；建议（正式用语）

collocations.zh: 过于理想化、难以照办的忠告

senses.title: Advice given to someone
senses.definition: formal advice offered to help someone decide or act
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助他人决定或行动而给出的正式建议
senses.example: The old judge gave the young clerk a piece of counsel he never forgot.
senses.exampleCN: 老法官给了年轻书记员一句他终生不忘的忠告。
senses.why: The core noun is the advice itself, an uncountable mass, which is why it is given and taken rather than counted one by one.
senses.whyCN: 核心名词就是建议本身，是不可数的整体，所以它是被「给出」和「采纳」的，而不是被一条条计数的。

senses.title: The act of deliberating together
senses.definition: consultation or deliberation with others before acting
senses.definitionCN: 行动之前与他人的商议与斟酌
senses.example: After much counsel with his partners, he withdrew the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 与合伙人反复商议后，他撤回了请求。
senses.why: Advice is also an activity: people take counsel together, so the noun names the meeting as well as the words spoken in it.
senses.whyCN: 建议也是一种活动：人们会一起商议，所以这个名词既指说出口的话，也指那场会。

senses.title: A legal adviser
senses.definition: a person whose profession is to give legal advice
senses.definitionCN: 以提供法律意见为职业的人
senses.example: The queen's counsel advised her on the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 女王的法律顾问就条约向她进言。
senses.why: Because the most valued advice is legal, the noun came to stand for the adviser himself, first in royal service and then in general practice.
senses.whyCN: 因为最被看重的建议是法律意见，这个名词便转而指提供意见的人，先在王室服务中出现，后来进入一般执业。

senses.title: The advocates on one side
senses.definition: the lawyer or team of lawyers appearing for a party in a case
senses.definitionCN: 在案件中代表一方的律师或律师团队
senses.example: Counsel for the defence rose to cross-examine the witness.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方律师起身盘问证人。
senses.why: In court the adviser becomes the speaker, and the word serves as a collective name for the legal team on one side of the case.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，顾问变成了发言者，这个词就用作案中一方律师团队的集体名称。

senses.title: To advise someone
senses.definition: to give someone advice about what to do
senses.definitionCN: 就该怎么做向某人提出建议
senses.example: She counselled him to wait a week before responding.
senses.exampleCN: 她劝他等一周再回应。
senses.why: The verb turns the noun into an act; the advice is now something one person does to another rather than something held.
senses.whyCN: 动词把名词变成动作：建议这时是一个人加于另一个人的行为，而不再是握有之物。

senses.title: To advise against something
senses.definition: to recommend that something should not be done
senses.definitionCN: 建议不要做某事
senses.example: The doctor counselled against surgery at his age.
senses.exampleCN: 医生劝他这把年纪不要动手术。
senses.why: Advice often takes the form of a warning, and the fixed preposition marks the negative direction of the recommendation.
senses.whyCN: 建议常以警告的形式出现，固定搭配中的介词标出了这条建议的否定方向。

senses.title: To keep one's own counsel
senses.definition: to keep one's plans or opinions secret
senses.definitionCN: 不泄露自己的打算或看法
senses.example: He kept his own counsel until the audit was complete.
senses.exampleCN: 审计结束之前，他一直守口如瓶。
senses.why: If counsel is advice, keeping it to oneself means not disclosing one's plan, so the phrase slid from advice toward silence.
senses.whyCN: 既然 counsel 是建议，把它留在自己这里就等于不吐露打算，于是这个说法从「建议」滑向了「沉默」。

senses.title: A settled plan or decree
senses.definition: in older and religious prose, a settled purpose or decree
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本与宗教文字中，指既定的意图或旨意
senses.example: The chronicler wrote that the king's counsel could not be overturned.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史作者写道，国王的谋划无法被推翻。
senses.why: Deliberation produces a fixed plan, and older writing uses the noun for that outcome, a sense now confined to formal and scriptural style.
senses.whyCN: 商议会产生固定的计划，较早的文字便用这个名词指那个结果；这一含义如今只留在正式与经文文体中。

intro.en: Counsel comes from Latin consilium 'advice, deliberation', the noun of consulere 'to consult'. It is not related to consul, the title of an official, although the two look alike. The deeper origin of consulere is source uncertain.
intro.cn: counsel 来自拉丁 consilium「建议、商议」，是动词 consulere「咨询」的名词。它与表示官职的 consul 无关，虽然两者外形相似。consulere 的更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Consulere meant to consult, to take counsel and to deliberate. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the Indo-European connections sometimes suggested for it remain reconstructions.
items.cn: consulere 意为咨询、商议、斟酌。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的印欧语关联仍属重构。

items.en: Consilium was the noun of the act: advice, a plan, and also a body of advisers. The noun, not the title consul, is the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: consilium 是这个动作的名词：建议、计划，也指一群顾问。英语这个词的直接来源是这个名词，而不是官职 consul。

items.en: French conseil kept both the advice and the body of advisers, and English borrowed it after the Norman conquest along with much legal vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语 conseil 同时保留「建议」与「顾问群体」两义，英语在诺曼征服后连同大量法律词汇一起借入。

items.en: Middle English counsel covered advice, secrecy, deliberation and the legal adviser, a range still visible today in fixed phrases.
items.cn: 中古英语的 counsel 覆盖建议、保密、商议与法律顾问，这一范围至今仍能在固定说法中看到。

items.en: In court practice counsel became the standard name for the barrister appearing for a party, giving the phrases counsel for the prosecution and counsel for the defence.
items.cn: 在法庭实务中，counsel 成为代表一方出庭的律师的标准称呼，因而有了控方律师与辩方律师这类说法。

items.en: Modern English keeps the legal sense in court reporting and the advice sense in formal writing, while the everyday verb survives mainly in warnings and recommendations.
items.cn: 现代英语在法庭报道中保留法律义，在正式写作中保留建议义；日常的动词用法主要留在警告与推荐里。

note.en: Group one separates two famous look-alikes with different Latin sources; group two sets the word against its everyday synonyms and its professional neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组分出两个著名的形近词，它们的拉丁来源并不相同；第二组把这个词与日常同义词、职业近邻作对照。

entries.definition: An assembly or its members, from Latin concilium 'meeting'; counsel comes from consilium 'advice'. The two are pronounced alike and spelled differently.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会或其成员，来自拉丁 concilium「集会」；counsel 来自 consilium「建议」。两者读音相同，拼写不同。

entries.definition: An official, either a Roman magistrate or a diplomat abroad; it is not the source of counsel and has no sense of advice.
entries.definitionCN: 指官员，或罗马执政官，或驻外领事；它不是 counsel 的来源，也没有建议之义。

entries.definition: The person who gives counsel; the base noun can name the advice itself or a legal team.
entries.definitionCN: 提供建议的人；基础名词既可指建议本身，也可指一支律师团队。

entries.definition: The activity of giving guidance, especially therapeutic guidance, not the advice as content.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供指导的活动，尤指心理辅导，而不是建议的内容。

entries.definition: A member of a council, built on council rather than on counsel; the doubled l and the different base keep the two apart.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会成员，构词基础是 council 而非 counsel；双写 l 与不同的基础词把两者分开。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for a recommendation; counsel is more formal and carries deliberation or legal weight.
entries.definitionCN: 指建议的日常词；counsel 更正式，带商议或法律分量。

entries.definition: To recommend what someone should do; the verb counsel is formal and often implies authority or care.
entries.definitionCN: 劝某人该怎么做；动词 counsel 更正式，常含权威或关怀意味。

entries.definition: Advice aimed at direction over time, especially for students; counsel can be a single consultation or a legal role.
entries.definitionCN: 长期方向性的指导，尤指对学生；counsel 可以是一次咨询，也可以是一个法律角色。

entries.definition: The neutral name for a legal practitioner; counsel names the adviser in a formal or courtroom setting.
entries.definitionCN: 法律执业者的中性称呼；counsel 指正式或法庭场景中的顾问。

entries.definition: The American formal word for a legal representative; counsel is broader and can also mean the advice itself.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法；counsel 范围更广，也可指建议本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin noun, the real look-alikes and the real legal phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁名词、真实的形近词与真实的法庭说法。

normal.en: Consilium is advice; concilium is a meeting. One letter of difference in Latin becomes council versus counsel in English.
normal.cn: consilium 是建议，concilium 是集会。拉丁语差一个字母，英语里就成了 council 与 counsel。

normal.en: Consul is a title, not a source: an official gives orders, a counsel gives advice.
normal.cn: consul 是官职，不是来源：官员下命令，顾问给建议。

normal.en: The word can be the advice, the adviser and the advising, all in one form.
normal.cn: 这个词可以是建议、顾问，也可以是劝告这件事，全都同一个形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: take counsel, keep one's own counsel, counsel for the defence.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：商议、守口如瓶、辩方律师。

normal.en: The verb keeps a warning tone: doctors and lawyers counsel against risky steps.
normal.cn: 动词保留警告语气：医生与律师都会劝人不要走冒险的那一步。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs by a fire, one person talking and one listening, with a sealed letter on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象炉火边两把椅子，一人在说、一人在听，桌上放着一封封好的信。

abstract.en: Picture advice as a heavy object that can be given, taken, kept or weighed.
abstract.cn: 想象建议是一件有重量的东西，可以给出、采纳、留存或称量。

abstract.en: Picture a room where the person who speaks is also the person who is named by the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间：说话的那个人，正是这个词所指的那个人。

examples.en: She took counsel from three retired judges before filing the appeal.
examples.cn: 提起上诉前，她征询了三位退休法官的意见。

examples.en: Counsel for the prosecution opened with a single sentence.
examples.cn: 控方律师用一句话开了场。

examples.en: He counselled patience when everyone else demanded an answer.
examples.cn: 所有人都要答案时，他劝大家耐心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠诉」——遇事靠诉讼前，先找人把话说清楚 → 建议、法律顾问

root: 拉丁 consilium（建议、商议）与 consulere（咨询、斟酌）；与官职 consul 无关，consulere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from advice itself, through deliberation, the adviser, the courtroom team, the verb of advising, the warning against something, the keeping of silence, and the older sense of a settled plan.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从建议本身开始，经商议、顾问、庭上的律师团队、劝告这个动词、劝阻某事、守口如瓶，最后到较早文本中「既定谋划」的含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed letter kept on the table while two people weigh the options.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上放着一封封好的信，两个人在权衡取舍。

branches.en: THE CONTENT: advice as an uncountable thing that one gives and another takes.
branches.cn: 内容：建议作为不可数之物，一个人给出，另一个人采纳。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: deliberation turns the same noun into an activity shared by several people.
branches.cn: 过程：商议让同一个名词变成多人共享的活动。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE TEAM: legal advice produces both the named adviser and the collective counsel on one side of a case.
branches.cn: 人与团队：法律意见既产生具名的顾问，也产生案中一方那支被称为 counsel 的队伍。

branches.en: THE ACT: the verb advises and, with against, warns away from a step.
branches.cn: 动作：动词表示劝告，带上反对介词则把人从某一步劝开。

branches.en: THE HELD PLAN: advice kept silent becomes secrecy, and deliberation settled becomes a decree.
branches.cn: 握住的计划：建议被留在心里就成了保密，商议定下结果就成了旨意。

intro.en: Counsel is a Latin noun that arrived through French, with a verb beside it and a large derived family in English.
intro.cn: counsel 是经法语传入的拉丁名词，旁边配着一个动词，并在英语里长出一大族派生词。

latinIntro.en: The base is consulere 'to consult' plus the noun ending -ium; the agent ending -or later built counselor, and the English ending -ing built counselling.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是 consulere「咨询」加名词词尾 -ium；施事后缀 -or 后来构成 counselor，英语的 -ing 构成 counselling。

items.meaningCN: 共同、一起（前缀表示聚合）
items.example: The prefix pictures people gathered to talk.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀描绘人们聚在一起商谈。

items.meaningCN: 咨询；斟酌
items.exampleCN: 这个动词命名「求教」这一动作。

items.meaning: result or thing of an act
items.meaningCN: 动作的结果或事物（名词后缀把动作转成实体）
items.example: The suffix made a noun of the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 建议；计划；顾问团（由动作转为内容与群体）
items.example: Consilium meant the advice and the advisers.
items.exampleCN: consilium 既指建议，也指顾问。

items.meaningCN: 建议；顾问会议（经法语转写）
items.exampleCN: 法语把两个含义都保留了。

items.structure: conseil used as an English noun
items.meaningCN: 建议或法律顾问（进入英语后一形兼两义）
items.exampleCN: 顾问向当事人提出建议。

items.meaningCN: 做某事的人（施事后缀把动作转成施事者）
items.example: Counselor is the person who counsels.
items.exampleCN: counselor 就是提供建议的人。

items.meaningCN: 提供指导的活动（动名词后缀把动作转成持续的活动）

definition_zh: 顾问；辅导员；心理咨询师；（美国）律师；外交参赞
definition_en: a person who gives guidance, especially in law, education or mental health
core_image: 安静的办公室里，桌对面的人把纸巾盒往前推了推，墙上贴着课程表和一排值班姓名
scene: 开学第一周，一名新生因为选课和想家坐在指导老师对面，话没说完就红了眼眶。The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
sceneCN: 这里 counselor 指学校里负责学业与生活指导的老师（第 4 个义项：学校辅导员）；句意：这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。图中可辨识物件：纸巾盒、课程表、值班表、两把椅子。

pos.zh: 顾问；提供指导的人
（美国）律师
心理咨询师；辅导员
（外交）参赞

senses.title: A person who gives guidance
senses.definition: someone whose role is to advise another person
senses.definitionCN: 职责是向他人提出建议的人
senses.example: A counselor listened to the whole story before saying anything.
senses.exampleCN: 这位顾问听完整个来龙去脉才开口。
senses.why: The agent ending marks the person who does the advising, so the noun is the human counterpart of counsel as advice.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀标记做这件事的人，所以这个名词是「建议」的人形对应物。

senses.title: A lawyer in American usage
senses.definition: in American English, a lawyer who advises clients and may appear in court
senses.definitionCN: 在美式英语中，指为客户提供咨询、也可出庭的律师
senses.example: The counselor filed the motion on behalf of the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师代表遗产一方提交了动议。
senses.why: Legal advice is the oldest branch of the trade, and American usage keeps the title for practising lawyers, especially in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 法律咨询是这门行业最古老的一支，美式用法把这个称谓留给执业律师，尤其在正式文书中。

senses.title: A therapist or mental health counselor
senses.titleCN: 心理咨询师；心理治疗师
senses.definition: a trained professional who helps people with emotional or psychological difficulties
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、帮助人们处理情绪或心理困难的专业人员
senses.example: She saw a counselor twice a month after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后，她每月见两次心理咨询师。
senses.why: The twentieth century widened the word from legal advice to therapeutic guidance, because both are forms of structured talk.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪把这个词从法律建议扩展到心理辅导，因为两者都是有结构的谈话。

senses.title: A school or college adviser
senses.titleCN: 学校辅导员；学业指导员
senses.definition: a staff member who guides students on courses, applications and personal problems
senses.definitionCN: 指导学生选课、申请与个人问题的教职员工
senses.example: The counselor helped the freshman choose courses and adjust to campus life.
senses.exampleCN: 这位辅导员帮新生选课，并适应校园生活。
senses.why: Schools needed someone between teacher and administrator, and the title transferred from law to education with the idea of guidance intact.
senses.whyCN: 学校需要一个介于教师与管理者之间的人，这个称谓便从法律转到教育，而「指导」这个观念原样保留。

senses.title: A camp counselor
senses.definition: a supervisor who looks after young campers and leads activities
senses.definitionCN: 照看年轻营员、带领活动的带队人员
senses.example: Each cabin of eight children shared one counselor.
senses.exampleCN: 每间住八个孩子的营房配一名辅导员。
senses.why: Supervision of the young is a form of guidance, so seasonal camps borrowed the same title for a temporary role.
senses.whyCN: 照看年轻人本身就是一种指导，所以季节性营地也用同一个称谓来指临时岗位。

senses.title: A diplomatic counselor
senses.definition: a senior officer at an embassy who handles a specialised area
senses.definitionCN: 使馆中负责某一专门领域的资深官员
senses.example: The cultural counselor arranged the exchange of students.
senses.exampleCN: 文化参赞安排了学生的互访。
senses.why: Diplomatic ranks adopted the word for an official who advises an ambassador within one field, keeping the advisory core.
senses.whyCN: 外交衔级采用这个词，指在某一领域向大使提供建议的官员，保留了「顾问」的内核。

senses.title: Counselor at law
senses.definition: a formal historical title for a licensed lawyer
senses.definitionCN: 历史上对持照律师的正式称谓
senses.example: The sign outside his office read counselor at law.
senses.exampleCN: 他办公室外的招牌上写着「执业律师」。
senses.why: The compound fixed the rank in a title, and the phrase survives on old brass plates long after ordinary speech dropped it.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合结构把身份固定成一个头衔，普通口语早已不用，它却还能在旧铜牌上见到。

senses.title: A specialist adviser in an organisation
senses.definition: an adviser attached to a body to cover one technical area, such as finance or genetics
senses.definitionCN: 受聘于某一机构、负责一个技术领域的顾问，如财务或遗传
senses.example: A genetic counselor explained the test results to the couple.
senses.exampleCN: 遗传咨询师向这对夫妇解释了检测结果。
senses.why: As knowledge specialised, organisations appointed advisers with a field label in front of the title, a pattern the word still follows.
senses.whyCN: 随着知识专门化，机构开始任命前面带领域标签的顾问，这个词至今仍循着这个模式。

intro.en: Counselor is counsel plus the agent ending -or, which comes from Latin -or. The base noun goes back to Latin consilium 'advice', and the American spelling with one l contrasts with British counsellor.
intro.cn: counselor 是 counsel 加施事后缀 -or，后者来自拉丁 -or。基础名词上溯拉丁 consilium「建议」，美式单 l 的拼法与英式 counsellor 相对。

items.en: Consilium meant advice, a plan or a body of advisers. It is the noun of consulere 'to consult', and not a form of the official title consul.
items.cn: consilium 指建议、计划或一群顾问。它是动词 consulere「咨询」的名词，而不是官职 consul 的形式。

items.en: The suffix -or marked the person who performs an action, as in doctor and victor. It gave English the shape of counselor, the one who gives the counsel.
items.cn: 后缀 -or 标记执行动作的人，如 doctor、victor。它给了英语 counselor 这个形态，即提供建议的人。

items.en: English first used counsel for the advice and for the adviser, before the agent ending was added to make the person explicit.
items.cn: 英语最初用 counsel 既指建议也指顾问，之后才加上施事后缀，把人明确标出。

items.en: Counselor was formed inside English rather than borrowed whole, which is why the British and American spellings differ: counsellor and counselor.
items.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的，而不是整体借入，所以英美拼写不同：counsellor 与 counselor。

items.en: Guidance work in schools and therapeutic work in clinics adopted the title during the twentieth century, widening it far beyond law.
items.cn: 二十世纪，学校的指导工作与诊所的治疗工作采用了这个称谓，使它远远超出法律领域。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for legal advisers, school advisers, therapists and camp staff, with the context deciding which role is meant.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指法律顾问、学校指导员、心理治疗师与营地带队人员，由语境决定所指的角色。

note.en: Group one separates the base word, the spelling variant and two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the person against other helping roles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词、拼写变体，与两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把这个人同其他助人角色作对照。

entries.definition: The advice itself or a legal team; counselor is always the person who gives the guidance.
entries.definitionCN: 指建议本身或一支律师团队；counselor 则始终指提供指导的人。

entries.definition: The same word spelled with double l in British English; the meaning does not change.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词在英式英语中的双 l 拼法，含义不变。

entries.definition: A member of a council or local assembly, built on council 'meeting'; it is not an adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 指议会或地方议会的成员，构词基础是 council「集会」；它不是顾问。

entries.definition: A diplomatic or Roman official; the word shares sounds with counsel but has a separate origin and no advisory sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指外交或罗马官员；读音与 counsel 相近，来源不同，也无顾问之义。

entries.definition: The activity of giving guidance; the counselor is the person who performs it.
entries.definitionCN: 指提供指导的活动；counselor 是从事这项活动的人。

entries.definition: A broad word for anyone who gives recommendations; counselor often implies training or a formal role.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指提出建议的人；counselor 常暗示受过训练或有正式职位。

entries.definition: A trained practitioner who treats mental or physical conditions; a counselor may advise without clinical treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗身心问题的受训执业者；counselor 可能只提供咨询而不做临床治疗。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a legal practitioner; counselor is the American formal title for the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 法律执业者的日常说法；counselor 是同一角色的美国正式称谓。

entries.definition: A formal American term for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: An experienced person who guides another over time; a counselor usually works within a defined role or session.
entries.definitionCN: 以经验长期引导他人的人；counselor 通常在一个明确的角色或会谈框架内工作。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent ending, the real legal sense and the real British spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施事后缀、真实的法律义与真实的英式拼写。

normal.en: Counsel plus the agent ending -or gives the person whose job is the advising.
normal.cn: counsel 加施事后缀 -or，得到以「提建议」为职责的那个人。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the l: counsellor, while the American keeps one.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，写作 counsellor；美式只写一个 l。

normal.en: Councilor is a council member, not an adviser: the base word is council, a meeting.
normal.cn: councilor 是议会成员，不是顾问：它的基础词是 council，即集会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the setting: school counselor, marriage counselor, camp counselor.
normal.cn: 固定说法点明场景：学校辅导员、婚姻咨询师、夏令营辅导员。

normal.en: In American formal writing the word still means a lawyer, as in counselor at law.
normal.cn: 在美国正式文书中，这个词仍指律师，如「执业律师」这一旧称。

abstract.en: Picture a tissue box pushed across a desk, a timetable on the wall behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒纸巾被推过桌面，身后墙上贴着课程表。

abstract.en: Picture a title that fits a courtroom, a classroom and a clinic without changing its shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一个不用改变外形就能嵌进法庭、教室与诊室的称谓。

abstract.en: Picture a person whose only tool is structured talk, given at a fixed hour each week.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人唯一的工具是有结构的谈话，每周在固定时间进行。

examples.en: The counselor asked one more question and then stayed quiet.
examples.cn: 辅导员又问了一个问题，然后安静下来。

examples.en: A camp counselor must know every child by name.
examples.cn: 夏令营辅导员必须叫得出每个孩子的名字。

examples.en: The embassy counselor handled the visa dispute.
examples.cn: 使馆参赞处理了那桩签证纠纷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「靠啥了」——心里没底就找顾问问一问「靠啥了」→ 辅导员、顾问

root: 英语 counsel（建议、法律顾问，源自拉丁 consilium）加施事后缀 -or（源自拉丁 -or），指提供指导的人；英式拼作 counsellor。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the general adviser, through the American lawyer, the therapist, the school adviser, the camp supervisor, the diplomatic rank, the old title at law, and the specialist adviser inside an organisation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从泛称顾问开始，经美国律师、心理治疗师、学校辅导员、夏令营带队人、外交参赞、旧时的执业律师头衔，最后到机构内的专科顾问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a desk with a tissue box and a timetable, one person listening.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张放着纸巾盒与课程表的桌子，一个人在那里倾听。

branches.en: THE ROLE: the agent ending turns advice into a person whose job it is.
branches.cn: 角色：施事后缀把「建议」变成以此为职的人。

branches.en: THE LAW: the oldest field of advice supplies the American legal title.
branches.cn: 法律：最古老的咨询领域提供了美国的律师称谓。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: structured talk about feelings becomes a therapeutic profession.
branches.cn: 诊室：围绕情绪的有结构谈话，成为一门治疗职业。

branches.en: THE YOUNG: schools and camps appoint adults to guide students and campers.
branches.cn: 年轻人：学校与营地都安排成年人去指导学员与营员。

branches.en: THE FORMAL TITLES: embassies, old legal brass plates and specialised desks all keep the advisory core in a title.
branches.cn: 正式头衔：使馆、旧日的律师铜牌与专科岗位，都以头衔形式保留「顾问」的内核。

intro.en: Counselor is an English-built agent noun on a borrowed base, so its ending is the part that says 'the person'.
intro.cn: counselor 是在英语内部构成的施事名词，基础词是借来的，词尾才是表示「那个人」的部分。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is consilium 'advice' from consulere 'to consult'; the Latin agent suffix -or supplies the ending, and the spelling -our marks the British form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁基础是 consilium「建议」，出自 consulere「咨询」；拉丁施事后缀 -or 提供词尾，而 -our 拼法标出英式形式。

items.meaningCN: 咨询；斟酌
建议；计划；顾问团
执行动作的人（施事后缀）
items.example: Doctor and victor share the ending.
items.exampleCN: doctor 与 victor 共享这个词尾。

items.structure: consilium used as an English noun
items.meaningCN: 建议；法律顾问（借入后一形兼两义）
提供指导的人（在英语内部由基础词加施事后缀构成）
提供指导的活动（动名词后缀把动作转成持续的工作）

items.meaning: spelling variant with no change of meaning
items.meaningCN: 英式拼法变体，含义不变（同一词尾的书写差异）
执业律师（固定头衔把顾问义限定到法律职业）
items.example: The plate read counselor at law.

definition_zh: 被告；被起诉或被指控的一方；（旧）辩护者
definition_en: the party against whom a claim or a charge is brought
core_image: 被告席前一个人站着，桌上摊着起诉书，背后是旁听席，法官的目光正落在他身上
scene: 开庭那天，被指控的一方站在席位前，手里攥着起诉书副本，逐条否认。The defendant denied every charge read aloud in court.
sceneCN: 这里 defendant 指案件中被指控、被起诉的一方（第 1 个义项：刑事被告）；句意：这名被告对庭上宣读的每一项指控都予以否认。图中可辨识物件：被告席、起诉书副本、法官席、旁听席。

pos.zh: 被告（刑事案件中被指控者，或民事案件中被起诉者）
（旧）防守者；辩护者

collocations.phrase: the defendant in a criminal case

senses.title: The accused in a criminal case
senses.definition: the person charged with an offence and required to answer it in court
senses.definitionCN: 被控犯罪、必须在法庭上作出答辩的人
senses.example: The defendant denied every charge read aloud in court.
senses.exampleCN: 被告对庭上宣读的每一项指控都予以否认。
senses.why: The word is the present participle of the verb 'to defend', so the accused is literally the one doing the defending in the legal contest.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是动词「辩护」的现在分词，所以被告字面上就是在这场法律较量中「进行防守」的那一方。

senses.title: The party sued in a civil case
senses.definition: the party against whom a civil claim is brought
senses.definitionCN: 被提起民事请求的一方
senses.example: The defendant company argued that the contract had never been signed.
senses.exampleCN: 被告公司辩称那份合同从未签署。
senses.why: Civil and criminal procedure share the same structure of claim and answer, so one word serves both sides of the court system.
senses.whyCN: 民事与刑事程序共享「请求—答辩」的同一结构，所以一个词就覆盖了法院体系的两侧。

senses.title: The answering party, neutrally
senses.definition: the party that must respond to any formal claim, without implying guilt
senses.definitionCN: 必须对任何正式请求作出回应的一方，不含罪责暗示
senses.example: Each defendant was given a copy of the petition.
senses.exampleCN: 每一位应诉方都拿到了一份请求书副本。
senses.why: Procedure needs a neutral label for the side that answers, and the word supplies it without the moral weight of 'guilty'.
senses.whyCN: 程序需要一个中性的标签来指作答的一方，这个词正好提供，而不带「有罪」的道德重量。

senses.title: The party carrying the burden of answer
senses.definition: the party who must meet the claim with evidence and argument
senses.definitionCN: 必须以证据和论证来应对请求的一方
senses.example: As defendant, the hospital had to show that its staff had followed procedure.
senses.exampleCN: 作为被告，医院必须证明其员工遵守了程序。
senses.why: Once a claim is filed, the burden of answering shifts to this party, so the word also marks who must produce the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 请求一旦提出，作答的责任就转到这一方，所以这个词也标记谁必须拿出证据。

senses.title: The second name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在后面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named after the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式的案件名称中，排在「诉」之后的那一方
senses.example: In the report the defendant appeared second in the case name.
senses.exampleCN: 在报道中，被告排在案件名称的第二位。
senses.why: Court practice fixes the order of names, and the second slot marks the party being complained against, a convention the word now encodes.
senses.whyCN: 法庭实务固定了名称顺序，第二个位置标记被投诉的一方，这个词如今就编码了这一惯例。

senses.title: A defender in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中的防守者、辩护者
senses.definition: in older texts, a person who defends a place, a cause or another person
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指守卫某地、某项事业或他人的人
senses.example: The chronicle names him as the defendant of the northern wall.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称他为北墙的守卫者。
senses.why: Before it became a courtroom label, the participle simply meant the one defending, in war or in argument, and older writing keeps that sense.
senses.whyCN: 在成为法庭标签之前，这个分词只表示「正在防守的人」，无论战阵还是辩论，较早文本保留了这一含义。

senses.title: Anyone who must answer criticism
senses.definition: figuratively, a person or body put in the position of answering a public charge
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义上，被置于公开指控之下、必须作答的个人或机构
senses.example: The minister found himself the defendant in a public inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位部长发现自己在公开调查中成了被质询的一方。
senses.why: Because the legal frame is so familiar, it transfers to public argument, where the accused side must answer before an audience.
senses.whyCN: 因为法律框架太熟悉，它便转移到公共争论中：被指控的一方要在众人面前作答。

senses.title: The responding party in a tribunal
senses.titleCN: 仲裁或裁判庭中的应诉方
senses.definition: the party answering a claim in arbitration or an administrative tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 在仲裁或行政裁判庭中应对请求的一方
senses.example: The defendant in the arbitration agreed to a private hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁中的应诉方同意进行不公开听证。
senses.why: Courts are not the only forum, and the word travels to any body that hears a claim and expects an answer.
senses.whyCN: 法院并非唯一的场域，这个词也适用于任何受理请求并要求答辩的机构。

intro.en: Defendant is the Old French present participle of defendre, from Latin defendere 'to ward off'. The verb joins de- 'away' with fendere 'to strike', the same second element seen in offend. The deeper origin of fendere is source uncertain.
intro.cn: defendant 是古法语 defendre 的现在分词，源自拉丁 defendere「挡开」。这个动词由 de-「离开」与 fendere「击打」构成，后半与 offend 共享。fendere 的更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Fendere meant to strike or push. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the connections sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions rather than settled derivations.
items.cn: fendere 意为击打、推。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的关联只是重构，并非已定的派生。

items.en: De- 'away' plus fendere gave defendere, 'to ward off, to repel, to protect'. The military image is a blow pushed aside.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 fendere 构成 defendere，意为挡开、击退、保护。军事意象是一记被推开的打击。

items.en: The same second element appears in offendere 'to strike against', the source of offend, which shows that fendere was a productive verb of striking.
items.cn: 同一个后半也出现在 offendere「撞击、冒犯」中，即 offend 的来源，说明 fendere 曾是一个能产的「击打」动词。

items.en: French defendre meant to defend, to protect and also to forbid, a range that English inherited in part through legal phrases.
items.cn: 法语 defendre 意为防守、保护，也意为禁止，这一范围部分经法律短语传入英语。

items.en: The present participle defendant meant 'the defending one' and was used as a noun in legal French for the party answering a charge.
items.cn: 现在分词 defendant 意为「正在辩护的那一个」，在法律法语中作名词，指对指控作出答辩的一方。

items.en: English dropped the military sense from ordinary speech and kept the procedural role, while the older idea survives in historical writing about defenders of a place.
items.cn: 英语在日常口语中丢掉了军事义，保住了程序角色；而「守卫某地者」的旧义仍留在历史文字里。

note.en: Group one separates the verb, the defender, the abstract case and a look-alike with a different source; group two sets the role against the other names used for people in a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词、防守者、抽象的案件名目，以及一个来源不同的形近词；第二组把这个角色与案中其他人的称呼作对照。

entries.definition: The act of answering a claim or protecting someone; the defendant is the person in that position.
entries.definitionCN: 指应对请求或保护他人的动作；defendant 是处于这个位置的人。

entries.definition: One who defends, often a protector; a defendant defends himself but is named by the claim against him.
entries.definitionCN: 指防守者，常含保护者意味；被告也为自己辩护，但他是按被指控的身份命名的。

entries.definition: The answer or the whole case for the accused; the defendant is the party, not the argument.
entries.definitionCN: 指答辩或被告方的整套主张；defendant 是当事方，不是论证本身。

entries.definition: Openly refusing to obey, from French defier 'to defy'; it looks like defendant but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 公开拒绝服从，来自法语 defier「挑战、违抗」；外形像 defendant，却出自另一个动词。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a separate role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是另一个角色。

entries.definition: The person charged with a crime, common in criminal reporting; defendant is the procedural term in court.
entries.definitionCN: 被控犯罪的人，常用于犯罪报道；defendant 是法庭上的程序用语。

entries.definition: The party who answers in an appeal, arbitration or divorce case; defendant belongs to first-instance court language.
entries.definitionCN: 在上诉、仲裁或离婚案件中作答的一方；defendant 属于一审法庭的用语。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit, claiming or answering; defendant names only the answering side.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方，原告或被告皆可；defendant 只指应诉的一方。

entries.definition: The party who brings the civil claim, the mirror image of the defendant.
entries.definitionCN: 提起民事请求的一方，正是被告的镜像。

entries.definition: The party who appeals a decision; at that stage the old labels of plaintiff and defendant give way.
entries.definitionCN: 对判决提起上诉的一方；到了这一阶段，原告与被告的旧标签就让位了。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin verb of warding off and the real procedural opposites.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「挡开」动词，以及真实的程序对立体。

normal.en: Defendere is to push a blow away: the defendant is the one who must push the claim away.
normal.cn: defendere 是把打击推开：被告就是必须把请求推开的那个人。

normal.en: Offend and defend share the striking verb: one strikes against, the other strikes away.
normal.cn: offend 与 defend 共享「击打」动词：一个撞上去，一个挡开。

normal.en: Defender is the protector, defendant is the accused: the same verb, two directions of attention.
normal.cn: defender 是保护者，defendant 是被指控者：同一个动词，注意力朝向两个方向。

normal.en: Defiant is a look-alike: it comes from a verb meaning to defy, not from the verb of warding off.
normal.cn: defiant 是形近词：它出自意为「违抗」的动词，而不是「挡开」的动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the pair: plaintiff and defendant, the defendant's plea, a co-defendant.
normal.cn: 固定说法展示这对关系：原告与被告、被告的答辩、同案被告。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand catching a thrown object: the hand is the defendant's whole job.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手接住抛来的东西：这只手就是被告的全部工作。

abstract.en: Picture a name written second on a courtroom docket, after the versus.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭日程表上第二个写下的名字，位于「诉」字之后。

abstract.en: Picture someone standing while everyone else sits, answering a document held in one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都坐着，只有一个人站着，手里拿着文件作答。

examples.en: The defendant chose to remain silent and let the lawyer speak.
examples.cn: 被告选择保持沉默，由律师发言。

examples.en: A co-defendant agreed to testify against the others.
examples.cn: 一名同案被告同意作证指控其他人。

examples.en: The court reminded the defendant that the burden of proof had not shifted.
examples.cn: 法院提醒被告，举证责任并未转移。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「地防等」——站在被告席上，得就地防守、等着对方出招 → 被告

root: 古法语 defendant（defendre 的现在分词，意为「正在辩护的」），源自拉丁 defendere（挡开、保护）= de-（离开）+ fendere（击打）。fendere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal accused, through the civil party sued, the neutral answering side, the bearer of the burden, the second name in a case title, the old defender, the public figure answering criticism, and the responding party in arbitration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事被告开始，经民事被诉方、中性的应诉方、承担答辩责任者、案件名称中的第二顺位、旧时的防守者、公开受质询者，最后到仲裁中的应诉方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand raised to catch a thrown object.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只举起的手，接住抛来的东西。

branches.en: THE TWO COURTS: the same answering role serves criminal charges and civil claims.
branches.cn: 两类法庭：同一个应诉角色既服务于刑事指控，也服务于民事请求。

branches.en: THE NEUTRAL LABEL: procedure needs a name for the answering side that carries no hint of guilt.
branches.cn: 中性标签：程序需要一个不含罪责暗示的名称来指作答的一方。

branches.en: THE WEIGHT: once a claim is filed, this party must produce evidence and argument.
branches.cn: 重量：请求一经提出，这一方就必须拿出证据与论证。

branches.en: THE ORDER OF NAMES: the second slot in a case title marks the party complained against.
branches.cn: 名称顺序：案件名称的第二格标记被投诉的一方。

branches.en: THE WIDER USE: the old defender, the public figure under criticism and the party in arbitration all keep the core of warding off a charge.
branches.cn: 更宽的用法：旧时的防守者、受公众指责的人物、仲裁中的应诉方，都保留「挡开指控」的内核。

intro.en: Defendant is a Latin participle used as a noun, so its ending marks the person in the act of defending.
intro.cn: defendant 是作名词使用的拉丁分词，词尾标记正在辩护的那个人。

latinIntro.en: The verb defendere is de- 'away' plus fendere 'to strike'; the present participle defendens supplies the English form, and the same striking verb also built offend.
latinIntro.cn: 动词 defendere 是 de-「离开」加 fendere「击打」；现在分词 defendens 提供英语形态，同一个「击打」动词也构成了 offend。

items.meaningCN: 离开、去掉（前缀表示把东西推开）
items.example: The prefix points the blow away from the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把打击指向身体之外。

items.meaningCN: 击打；推
挡开；保护（把打击推离自身）
items.example: The compound named the warding off.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名「挡开」。

items.meaningCN: 正在防守的（分词词尾标记动作进行中）
items.example: The participle named the one defending.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词命名正在防守的人。

items.structure: defendant (French participle used as a noun)
items.meaningCN: 对指控作答的人（分词名词化，由动作转为角色）
正在做某事的人（分词词尾把动作转成施事者）
items.example: A claimant is one who claims.
items.exampleCN: claimant 就是提出请求的人。

items.meaningCN: 答辩；防御（抽象名词词尾把动作转成事体）
防守者；保护者（英语施事后缀，与 -ant 的「被控方」形成对照）
items.example: The defender of the fort surrendered.

definition_zh: 原告；起诉方；提出请求的一方
definition_en: the party who brings a civil case against another
core_image: 一叠写满委屈的纸被推过桌面，第一页最上面写着「我要求」，对面的人只看不接
scene: 开庭前，提起诉讼的一方坐在走廊长椅上，把请求赔偿的清单又数了一遍。The plaintiff listed every loss in the claim before the hearing began.
sceneCN: 这里 plaintiff 指在民事案件中提起诉讼、要求救济的一方（第 1 个义项：提起民事诉讼的一方）；句意：开庭前，这名原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。图中可辨识物件：走廊长椅、赔偿清单、文件夹、法庭门。

pos.zh: 原告；起诉方（民事案件中提出请求的一方）

collocations.phrase: a plaintiff in a civil action

derivatives.zh: 诉苦；申诉（书面或旧式用法）

senses.title: The party who brings a civil case
senses.definition: the person or body that starts a civil action against another
senses.definitionCN: 对他人提起民事诉讼的个人或机构
senses.example: The plaintiff listed every loss in the claim before the hearing began.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，原告在请求书中逐项列出了所有损失。
senses.why: The word is built from the verb of complaining, so the party is named by the act of bringing a grievance before a court.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「诉苦」的动词构成，所以这一方是按「把委屈带到法院」这个动作来命名的。

senses.title: The complaining party, literally
senses.definition: literally, the one who complains; the older force of the word
senses.definitionCN: 字面上指诉苦的人，这是这个词较早的力道
senses.example: In the old record the plaintiff is simply called the complainant.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧档案里，原告干脆就被称作「申诉人」。
senses.why: The French participle meant 'complaining', and the legal role grew out of that plain human act of stating a grievance.
senses.whyCN: 这个法语分词本意就是「诉苦的」，法律角色正是从「说出委屈」这一平常举动中长出来的。

senses.title: The party who files first
senses.definition: the party whose filing starts the clock of the case
senses.definitionCN: 其立案动作使案件时间开始走表的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff filed on Monday, and the summons went out on Tuesday.
senses.exampleCN: 原告周一立案，传票周二就发出去了。
senses.why: Procedure assigns the first move to one side, and that move is what makes the other side a defendant.
senses.whyCN: 程序把第一步分给一方，而正是这一步使另一方成为被告。

senses.title: The party seeking a remedy
senses.definition: the party asking the court for money, an order or another remedy
senses.definitionCN: 向法院请求金钱、命令或其他救济的一方
senses.example: As plaintiff, the tenant asked for the return of the deposit.
senses.exampleCN: 作为原告，租客要求返还押金。
senses.why: A case exists because someone wants something from the court, and the word marks that side of the demand.
senses.whyCN: 案件之所以存在，是因为有人想从法院得到什么，这个词就标记提出要求的那一侧。

senses.title: The first name in a case title
senses.titleCN: 案件名称中排在前面的当事方
senses.definition: in the style 'A v. B', the party named before the versus
senses.definitionCN: 在「甲诉乙」式名称中，排在「诉」之前的那一方
senses.example: The reporter read the case name with the plaintiff first.
senses.exampleCN: 记者念出案件名称时，原告排在首位。
senses.why: Court style fixes the order, and the first slot belongs to the one who brought the complaint, a rule still visible in case citations.
senses.whyCN: 法庭体例固定了顺序，第一格属于提出申诉的人，这一规则至今仍能在案件引证中看到。

senses.title: The party with the initial burden
senses.definition: the party who must first prove the basic elements of the claim
senses.definitionCN: 必须先证明请求基本要件的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff had to prove that the signature was genuine.
senses.exampleCN: 原告必须证明那个签名是真的。
senses.why: Whoever asserts must prove, so the procedural word also marks the side that carries the first load of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 谁主张谁举证，所以这个程序用语也标记首先承担证据重量的一侧。

senses.title: The party who starts arbitration
senses.definition: the party who brings a claim before an arbitrator or tribunal
senses.definitionCN: 向仲裁员或裁判庭提出请求的一方
senses.example: The plaintiff in the arbitration was a supplier from abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 仲裁中的原告是一家境外供应商。
senses.why: The same claim-and-answer structure appears outside court, and the label follows the claimant into private forums.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「请求—答辩」结构出现在法院之外，这个标签便随请求人进入私人裁判场合。

senses.title: An accuser in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, anyone who publicly accuses another of wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指公开指控他人有错的人
senses.example: The pamphlet cast the widow as plaintiff against the guild.
senses.exampleCN: 那本小册子把这位寡妇写成了控告行会的原告。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to civil procedure, it named any accuser, and historical writing still uses that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄为民事程序之前，它指任何指控者，历史文字仍保留这一较宽的范围。

intro.en: Plaintiff comes from Old French plaintif 'complaining', from plainte 'complaint', from Latin planctus 'lamentation', the noun of plangere 'to beat the breast'. The legal sense grew from the plain act of stating a grievance.
intro.cn: plaintiff 来自古法语 plaintif「诉苦的」，经 plainte「申诉」上溯拉丁 planctus「哀号」，即 plangere「捶胸」的名词。法律义从「说出委屈」这一平常动作中生长出来。

items.en: Plangere meant to beat or strike, especially the breast in grief, and so to lament. Its deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: plangere 意为击打，尤指悲伤时捶胸，因而意为哀号。其更深来源属来源不确定。

items.en: Planctus was the noun of that beating and wailing: a lamentation, a loud complaint. It supplies the stem seen in plaintive and plaint.
items.cn: planctus 是「捶打与号哭」的名词：哀号、高声诉苦。它提供了 plaintive 与 plaint 中可见的词干。

items.en: Plainte meant a complaint or lament in French, covering both the sound of grief and the formal statement of a grievance.
items.cn: 法语 plainte 指申诉或哀诉，既指悲伤的声音，也指正式提出的不满。

items.en: The adjective plaintif meant 'complaining', and it could stand as a noun for the person who complains, the exact shape English borrowed.
items.cn: 形容词 plaintif 意为「诉苦的」，可作名词指诉苦的人，英语借入的正是这个形态。

items.en: From the fourteenth century English used plaintiff for the party who brings a complaint to court, pairing it with defendant.
items.cn: 十四世纪起，英语用 plaintiff 指把申诉带到法院的一方，并与 defendant 配对使用。

items.en: The word narrowed to civil procedure, where it means the party who sues, while the older sense of any accuser survives only in historical prose.
items.cn: 这个词收窄为民事程序用语，指提起诉讼的一方；而「任何指控者」的旧义只留在历史叙述中。

note.en: Group one separates the complaint, the sad adjective, the unrelated look-alike and the related word with another prefix; group two sets the role against the other names for a claimant.
note.cn: 第一组区分申诉本身、表示哀伤的形容词、无关的形近词，以及带另一个前缀的同根词；第二组把这个角色与请求人的其他称呼作对照。

entries.definition: A complaint or lament, especially in literary or older legal prose; plaintiff is the person, not the text.
entries.definitionCN: 指申诉或哀诉，多见于文学或较早的法律文字；plaintiff 是人，不是文本。

entries.definition: Sounding sad or mournful; it describes a tone, never a party in a case.
entries.definitionCN: 听起来哀伤的；它描述语气，从不指案件中的一方。

entries.definition: Simple or flat, from Latin planus 'flat'. It resembles plaint but has no connection with complaining.
entries.definitionCN: 简单的、平坦的，来自拉丁 planus「平」。它形似 plaint，却与诉苦毫无关系。

entries.definition: A grievance or its formal statement, from the same wailing verb with a prefix meaning 'together'; it is not the party.
entries.definitionCN: 指不满或其正式陈述，同出「哀号」动词，前缀意为「共同」；它不是当事方。

entries.definition: The possessive form marking something belonging to the party, not a second role.
entries.definitionCN: 所有格形式，表示属于该当事方之物，不是第二个角色。

entries.definition: The party making a claim, common in tribunals and benefit cases; plaintiff is the standard court term in civil suits.
entries.definitionCN: 提出请求的一方，常用于裁判庭与福利案件；plaintiff 是民事法庭的标准用语。

entries.definition: The party who files a petition, as in divorce or family cases, where the word often replaces plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 提交呈请书的一方，如在离婚或家事案件中，常用它代替 plaintiff。

entries.definition: The person who makes a complaint, sometimes the victim or the reporting party rather than the suing party.
entries.definitionCN: 提出投诉的人，有时指受害人或者报案人，而不一定是起诉方。

entries.definition: Any party to a lawsuit; plaintiff names only the side that brings the claim.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中的任何一方；plaintiff 只指提出请求的那一侧。

entries.definition: The party who must answer the claim, the mirror image of the plaintiff.
entries.definitionCN: 必须对请求作答的一方，正是原告的镜像。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real verb of wailing, the real look-alike plain and the real court pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「哀号」动词、真实的形近词 plain，以及真实的法庭配对。

normal.en: Plangere is to beat the breast: the plaintiff is the one who brings the lament to court.
normal.cn: plangere 是捶胸：原告就是把哀诉带进法院的那个人。

normal.en: Plain means flat, not complaining: one letter alike, two unrelated origins.
normal.cn: plain 意为平坦，不是诉苦；字母相近，来源却全不相干。

normal.en: Plaint is the complaint, plaintiff is the person, plaintive is the tone.
normal.cn: plaint 是申诉，plaintiff 是人，plaintive 是语气。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: plaintiff and defendant, claim and answer.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：原告与被告，请求与答辩。

normal.en: Whoever files first becomes the plaintiff and puts the other side in the answering seat.
normal.cn: 先立案的人成为原告，并把另一方放进应诉的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk, first line reading I demand.
abstract.cn: 想象一叠申诉纸被推过桌面，第一行写着「我要求」。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the first name on the docket is the one who spoke first.
abstract.cn: 想象一间法庭，日程表上的第一个名字，正是最先开口的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture grief turned into a document: the wail becomes a claim with numbered paragraphs.
abstract.cn: 想象悲伤被做成一份文件：号哭变成分条列项的请求。

examples.en: The plaintiff asked for the deposit back and won.
examples.cn: 原告要求返还押金，并且胜诉。

examples.en: A plaintiff must prove the elements of the claim one by one.
examples.cn: 原告必须逐项证明请求的各个要件。

examples.en: The plaintiff and the defendant agreed to mediate before trial.
examples.cn: 原告与被告在开庭前同意调解。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑泪啼夫」——哭着捶胸、把委屈递上法庭的那个人 → 原告

root: 古法语 plaintif（诉苦的），源自 plainte（申诉），上溯拉丁 planctus（哀号），即 plangere（捶胸、哀哭）的名词。plangere 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the civil claimant, through the literal complainer, the first filer, the seeker of a remedy, the first name in a title, the initial burden, the arbitration claimant, and the older accuser.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从民事原告开始，经字面的诉苦者、先立案者、寻求救济者、案件名称的首位、先负举证责任者、仲裁请求人，最后到较早的控诉者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of grievance sheets pushed across a desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠申诉纸被推过桌面。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: the legal party grows straight out of the plain act of complaining.
branches.cn: 来源：法律上的当事方直接由「诉苦」这一平常动作长成。

branches.en: THE FIRST MOVE: filing is what turns a grievance into a case.
branches.cn: 第一步：立案这个动作把委屈变成案件。

branches.en: THE DEMAND: the party is defined by what it asks the court to give.
branches.cn: 要求：这一方由它向法院请求什么来定义。

branches.en: THE PAPER AND THE PROOF: the first name in the title and the first load of evidence belong to the same side.
branches.cn: 文书与举证：名称的首位与第一批证据都属于同一侧。

branches.en: THE WIDER FORUMS: arbitration keeps the role, and older prose extends it to any accuser.
branches.cn: 更宽的场域：仲裁保留了这一角色，较早的文字则把它扩展到任何指控者。

intro.en: Plaintiff is a French adjective frozen into a legal noun, built on a Latin noun of wailing.
intro.cn: plaintiff 是一个冻结为法律名词的法语形容词，建立在拉丁「哀号」名词之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is plangere 'to beat the breast' and its noun planctus 'lamentation'; French added the adjective ending and English kept the whole shape.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是 plangere「捶胸」及其名词 planctus「哀号」；法语加上形容词词尾，英语把整个形态保留下来。

items.meaning: to beat, strike the breast, lament
items.meaningCN: 击打；捶胸；哀号
捶打；哀号（名词词尾把动作转成声音与事件）
申诉；哀诉（经法语转写）
倾向于……的（形容词后缀）
items.example: The suffix made the participle an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词干变成形容词。

items.meaningCN: 诉苦的（形容词化，随后可作名词）
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述诉苦的人。

items.structure: plaintif used as an English legal noun
items.meaning: the party who brings the complaint
items.meaningCN: 提出申诉的一方（形容词名词化，指案件中的角色）
申诉；哀诉（英语中缩短的形式）
哀伤的（形容词后缀把申诉转成语调）
items.example: A plaintive note ended the letter.
items.exampleCN: 信的结尾是一句哀伤的调子。

definition_zh: 起诉；检控；公诉方；诉讼的进行；（正式）从事、推行
definition_en: the act of bringing criminal charges and conducting the case against an accused
core_image: 一张长桌上摊开证据袋，桌后的人把材料一份接一份排成一条向前的线，桌对面还空着
scene: 警方把材料交到检方手里之后，案子从逮捕转入正式指控的阶段。The prosecution began as soon as the evidence file reached the state's lawyers.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecution 指对被告提起并推进刑事指控的过程（第 1 个义项：刑事起诉的程序）；句意：证据卷一交到州律师手中，公诉程序就开始了。图中可辨识物件：证据袋、长桌、卷宗、公诉席。

pos.zh: 起诉；检控；公诉（对被告提起并推进刑事程序）
公诉方；控方（代表国家起诉的一方）
（正式）从事、推行（某项工作或事业）

collocations.zh: 战争的进行（旧式正式说法）

senses.title: Criminal proceedings against an accused
senses.titleCN: 对被告的刑事起诉程序
senses.definition: the process of charging someone and pursuing the case in court
senses.definitionCN: 对某人提出指控并在法院推进案件的过程
senses.example: The prosecution began as soon as the evidence file reached the state's lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 证据卷一交到州律师手中，公诉程序就开始了。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow forward, and the legal noun pictures the state following a charge through every stage of a trial.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「向前追随」，这个法律名词描绘的正是国家把一项指控追随到审判的每一个阶段。

senses.title: The prosecuting authority
senses.definition: the body or office that has the power to bring charges
senses.definitionCN: 有权提出刑事指控的机构或部门
senses.example: The prosecution decided not to pursue the minor charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察机关决定不追究那项轻微的指控。
senses.why: An institution can stand for the act it performs, so the abstract noun also names the office that decides whether to charge.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以代表它所做的动作，所以这个抽象名词也指决定是否起诉的那个部门。

senses.title: The state's lawyers in court
senses.definition: the lawyers presenting the state's case in a particular trial
senses.definitionCN: 在具体审判中代表国家陈述案件的律师
senses.example: The prosecution sat on the left and the defence on the right.
senses.exampleCN: 控方坐在左边，辩方坐在右边。
senses.why: In courtroom speech the abstract noun becomes a collective label for the legal team on the charging side, like defence on the other side.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭用语里，这个抽象名词变成指控一侧律师团队的集体标签，正如另一侧被称为辩方。

senses.title: The decision to lay charges
senses.definition: the moment or act of formally charging a person
senses.definitionCN: 正式对某人提出指控的那一动作或时刻
senses.example: A prosecution at this stage would need stronger evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个阶段起诉，需要更有力的证据。
senses.why: The word covers the beginning as well as the whole case, because a charge is both a single decision and a long proceeding.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既覆盖开端，也覆盖整个案件，因为一次指控既是一个决定，也是一段漫长的程序。

senses.title: Formal carrying out of a task
senses.titleCN: 正式从事、推行某项工作
senses.definition: in formal writing, the carrying out or pursuit of an activity
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中，指对某项活动的推行与从事
senses.example: He was praised for the prosecution of his duties during the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 他因危机期间尽责履职而受到赞扬。
senses.why: The old sense of following something forward survives in formal prose, where any duty or study can be prosecuted, not only a crime.
senses.whyCN: 「把某事向前推进」的旧义在正式文字中保留下来：任何职责或研究都可以被「推行」，并不限于罪行。

senses.title: Pursuit or continuation of an undertaking
senses.titleCN: 事业或行动的继续推进
senses.definition: in older usage, the continued pursuit of a war, a policy or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，对战争、政策或计划的持续推进
senses.example: The history devotes a chapter to the prosecution of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这部史书用一章讲战争的进行。
senses.why: Before the word narrowed to law, it named any energetic continuation, and military and political writing kept that wider reach.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词收窄到法律之前，它指任何有力的持续推进，军事与政治文字保留了这一较宽的范围。

senses.title: The evidence stage of a trial
senses.definition: the part of a trial in which the charging side presents its evidence
senses.definitionCN: 审判中由指控方出示证据的那一部分
senses.example: During the prosecution, three experts described the damaged wall.
senses.exampleCN: 在控方举证阶段，三位专家描述了受损的墙体。
senses.why: Since the state speaks first, its phase of the trial takes the name of the whole proceeding, a part standing for the whole.
senses.whyCN: 因为国家一方先发言，审判中属于它的那个阶段便取了整个程序的名字，以部分代整体。

senses.title: Pursuit of a claim in older usage
senses.titleCN: 旧用法中对请求的追究
senses.definition: in older legal writing, the pursuing of any claim or suit
senses.definitionCN: 在较早法律文字中，对任何请求或诉讼的追究
senses.example: The record notes the prosecution of a debt against the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 档案记载了对该遗产的一笔债务追索。
senses.why: Civil claims were once prosecuted as well as criminal charges, and older documents use the noun for any claim pursued to judgment.
senses.whyCN: 民事请求一度与刑事指控一样被「追究」，较早文书便用这个名词指任何追究至判决的请求。

intro.en: Prosecution comes from Latin prosecutio, the noun of prosequi 'to follow forward', built from pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'to follow'. The oldest sense is continuation, and law narrowed it to the pursuit of a charge.
intro.cn: prosecution 来自拉丁 prosecutio，即 prosequi「向前追随」的名词，由 pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成。最古老的含义是「继续」，法律把它收窄为对指控的追究。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow. It also stands behind sequence, consecutive and the second half of prosecute, showing how widely the idea of following spread.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随。它也是 sequence、consecutive 以及 prosecute 后半的来源，可见「跟随」这一观念散布之广。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, to pursue, to continue'. In legal use it meant to pursue a charge or a claim.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。在法律用法中指追究一项指控或请求。

items.en: The noun prosecutio named the following or the pursuing, and could describe the continuation of any undertaking, not only a legal one.
items.cn: 名词 prosecutio 指追随或追究，可描述任何事业的继续，而不仅限于法律事务。

items.en: French legal usage applied the noun to the conduct of a case, and English borrowed it with that narrower focus already attached.
items.cn: 法语法律用法把这个名词用于案件进行，英语借入时已带着这一较窄的侧重。

items.en: English used prosecution for both the conduct of a criminal case and the carrying on of any business, keeping the two senses side by side for centuries.
items.cn: 英语用 prosecution 既指刑事案件的进行，也指任何事务的推行，两个含义并行了数百年。

items.en: Modern English centres the word on criminal proceedings, while the 'carrying out' sense survives in formal phrases about duties, studies or a war.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词的中心放在刑事程序上，而「推行」义保存在关于职责、研究或战争的正式说法里。

note.en: Group one separates the related verb and agent from a near look-alike with a hostile prefix and from a word that only shares spelling; group two sets the proceeding against the other names for a case.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根动词与施事者、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是拼写相近的词；第二组把这个程序与案件的其他名目作对照。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; prosecution is the proceeding as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecution 指整个程序。

entries.definition: The lawyer who conducts the case; the prosecution can also mean the team or the proceeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指推进案件的律师；prosecution 也可指团队或程序。

entries.definition: Systematic mistreatment, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix makes it harassment, not litigation.
entries.definitionCN: 系统性迫害，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀使它成为迫害，而不是诉讼。

entries.definition: A ban or outlawry, from proscribere 'to write up publicly'; it shares the opening letters but not the following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指禁令或剥夺公权，来自 proscribere「公开书写」；它与本词只共享开头字母，并不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Relating to a prosecutor or the conduct of a prosecution, not the proceeding itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与检察官或起诉行为有关的，不是程序本身。

entries.definition: The court hearing where evidence is tested; prosecution is the pursuing of the charge, which may end before trial.
entries.definitionCN: 指检验证据的庭审；prosecution 指对指控的追究，可能在开庭前就结束。

entries.definition: The whole matter before a court, civil or criminal; prosecution belongs to the criminal side.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交法院的整个事项，民事刑事皆可；prosecution 属刑事一侧。

entries.definition: The formal steps of a legal action; prosecution is the state's pursuit of a charge within them.
entries.definitionCN: 指法律行动的一系列正式步骤；prosecution 是其中对指控的国家追究。

entries.definition: The formal accusation itself, often after a grand jury; prosecution is the process that follows it.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指控文书本身，常在大陪审团之后；prosecution 是随后展开的程序。

entries.definition: A lawsuit in civil law or a military engagement; in legal speech it is broader and often civil.
entries.definitionCN: 指民事法中的诉讼，或军事行动；在法律用语中范围更广，且常指民事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb, the real hostile prefix and the real procedural pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词、真实的敌对前缀，以及真实的程序配对。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: the state follows its charge from filing to verdict.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：国家把指控从立案一路跟到判决。

normal.en: Persecution has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': one follows to court, the other follows to harm.
normal.cn: persecution 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀意为「贯穿」：一个跟到法院，一个跟到伤害。

normal.en: Proscription is a look-alike about public writing, not about following.
normal.cn: proscription 是形近词，讲的是公开书写，而不是跟随。

normal.en: The pair is fixed: the prosecution and the defence, charging side and answering side.
normal.cn: 这组配对是固定的：控方与辩方，指控一侧与答辩一侧。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture evidence bags laid end to end, forming a path toward an empty chair.
abstract.cn: 想象证据袋首尾相接，铺成一条通向空椅子的路。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a rope that the state keeps pulling, hand over hand, through every hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一根绳，国家一场庭审接一场庭审地双手交替往回拉。

abstract.en: Picture one side of a courtroom speaking first because the state is the one that complains.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭一侧先开口，因为提出申诉的是国家。

examples.en: The prosecution rested after four days of testimony.
examples.cn: 经过四天作证，控方结束了举证。

examples.en: Without the second witness, the prosecution would probably fail.
examples.cn: 若没有第二位证人，这场起诉很可能失败。

examples.en: He wrote a book on the prosecution of long wars.
examples.cn: 他写了一本关于长期战争如何进行的书。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究神」——把诉状层层剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的名词 prosecutio，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成；古义为「继续、推行」，后收窄为「起诉」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the criminal proceeding, through the authority, the courtroom team, the laying of charges, formal carrying out, the older continuation of an undertaking, the evidence stage, and the old pursuit of a claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从刑事程序开始，经检察机关、庭上的控方团队、提起指控、正式推行工作、旧时对事业的继续、举证阶段，最后到旧时对请求的追究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence bags laid end to end toward an empty chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：证据袋首尾相接，铺向一把空椅子。

branches.en: THE PROCEEDING: the state follows its charge through every stage of court.
branches.cn: 程序：国家把指控追随到法院的每一个阶段。

branches.en: THE THREE FACES: the authority, the team in court and the single decision to charge are one system seen at different distances.
branches.cn: 三张面孔：检察机关、庭上团队与提出指控的那一个决定，是同一系统在不同距离下的样子。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: any duty, study or war can be carried forward, which is what the verb meant before law took it over.
branches.cn: 旧义：任何职责、研究或战争都能被推行，这正是法律接管这个词之前它的意思。

branches.en: THE HEARING: the side that speaks first gives its name to the evidence stage.
branches.cn: 庭审：先发言的一侧把自己的名字给了举证阶段。

branches.en: THE WIDER CLAIM: older documents also prosecute debts and civil claims, not only crimes.
branches.cn: 更宽的请求：较早文书也「追究」债务与民事请求，并不限于罪行。

intro.en: Prosecution is a Latin action noun built on a verb of following, so it names a process rather than a person.
intro.cn: prosecution 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁动作名词，所以它命名的是过程，而不是人。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi 'follow' gives prosequi; the participle prosecutus and the noun prosecutio supply the stem, and -tion makes the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi「跟随」构成 prosequi；分词 prosecutus 与名词 prosecutio 提供词干，-tion 构成英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀给动作一个前进方向）
items.example: The prefix points the following forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「跟随」指向前方。

items.meaningCN: 跟随
向前追随；追求；继续
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词命名追究。

items.meaningCN: 已追究的（分词提供英语词干 prosecut-）
items.example: The participle supplied the English stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词提供了英语词干。

items.meaningCN: 动作或过程（名词后缀把动词转成程序名）
items.example: The suffix made a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成过程名词。

items.meaningCN: 对指控的追究（由动作转为整套程序）
推进案件的施事者（施事后缀把过程转成人）

items.meaning: to bring and conduct a case
items.meaningCN: 提起并推进案件（去掉名词词尾，回到动作）
与检察官有关的（形容词后缀把角色转成属性）

definition_zh: 检察官；公诉人；控方律师；（旧）执行者、追究者
definition_en: a lawyer who conducts criminal cases on behalf of the state
core_image: 一名公职律师站在公诉席后，面前是按编号排好的证据袋，身后墙上挂着国徽
scene: 庭审开始，公诉人站起来，先向法官概述证据，再请第一位证人上前。The prosecutor opened with a summary of the evidence and then called the first witness.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecutor 指代表国家出庭指控被告的检察官（第 1 个义项：代表国家提起公诉的律师）；句意：检察官先概述证据，然后传召第一位证人。图中可辨识物件：公诉席、编号证据袋、国徽、证人席。

pos.zh: 检察官；公诉人（代表国家提起并推进刑事案件的律师）
（旧）追行者；执行者

collocations.zh: 皇家检察官（英联邦用语）

senses.title: The state's lawyer in a criminal case
senses.titleCN: 刑事案件中代表国家的律师
senses.definition: a legal officer who brings and argues the state's case against an accused
senses.definitionCN: 代表国家对被告提起诉讼并出庭论证的公职律师
senses.example: The prosecutor opened with a summary of the evidence and then called the first witness.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官先概述证据，然后传召第一位证人。
senses.why: The agent ending turns the verb of pursuing into a person, so the prosecutor is literally the one who follows the charge forward.
senses.whyCN: 施事后缀把「追究」这个动词变成人，所以检察官字面上就是把指控向前追的那个人。

senses.title: The official who decides on charges
senses.definition: the public officer who reviews a file and decides whether to charge
senses.definitionCN: 审阅案卷并决定是否提出指控的公职官员
senses.example: The prosecutor read the file twice before authorising the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官把卷宗读了两遍才批准起诉。
senses.why: Not every accusation reaches court, and the office that screens files holds a gatekeeping power visible in this use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 并非每项指控都能进入法院，负责筛查卷宗的这个职位因此握有把门权，这一含义就体现在这种用法里。

senses.title: The side presenting evidence
senses.definition: the lawyer who presents the evidence against the accused at trial
senses.definitionCN: 在审判中出示不利于被告的证据的律师
senses.example: The prosecutor showed the jury the recording frame by frame.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官逐帧向陪审团展示了那段录像。
senses.why: Because the office speaks first in court, the person is identified with the presentation of proof.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个职位在法庭上先发言，这个人便与证据的呈现紧紧绑在一起。

senses.title: A rank inside a legal system
senses.titleCN: 法律体系内的一个职级
senses.definition: a titled post in a particular system, such as federal or district prosecutor
senses.definitionCN: 特定体系内带名号的职位，如联邦检察官或地区检察官
senses.example: She became the youngest federal prosecutor in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了该地区最年轻的联邦检察官。
senses.why: Different systems grade the office differently, so the word attaches to ranks and jurisdictions rather than to one uniform role.
senses.whyCN: 不同体系给这个职位定的级别不同，所以这个词会附着在级别与辖区上，而不是指一个统一的角色。

senses.title: An old sense: the pursuer or executor
senses.definition: in older texts, one who pursues or carries out an undertaking
senses.definitionCN: 在较早文本中，指追逐或执行某项事业的人
senses.example: The chronicle calls him the prosecutor of the king's justice.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史称他为国王司法事务的执行者。
senses.why: Before the word settled on criminal law, it named anyone who followed a task through to the end, a sense still readable in older prose.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词固定到刑法之前，它指任何把一项任务跟到底的人，这一含义在较早文字中仍可读出。

senses.title: The representative of the public
senses.definition: the official who acts in court for the public rather than for a private client
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上代表公众而非私人委托人行事的人
senses.example: The prosecutor reminded the court that the victim could not speak for herself.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官提醒法庭，受害人已无法为自己发声。
senses.why: The role exists because some wrongs are treated as harms to the whole community, so the lawyer speaks for a collective client.
senses.whyCN: 这个角色之所以存在，是因为某些侵害被视为对共同体的伤害，所以律师代表的是一个集体委托人。

senses.title: Anyone who brings an accusation, loosely
senses.definition: informally, any person or body that presses an accusation
senses.definitionCN: 非正式用法中，提出指控的任何个人或机构
senses.example: In the complaint the agency appears as prosecutor of the company's conduct.
senses.exampleCN: 在投诉书中，该机构成了公司行为的指控者。
senses.why: The word can leave the courtroom and name whoever is pushing a charge, a looser use common in journalism and campaigning.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以走出法庭，指任何推动一项指控的人，这一较松的用法在新闻与倡议文字中很常见。

senses.title: The opposing role in a criminal trial
senses.titleCN: 刑事审判中的对抗角色
senses.definition: the functional opposite of defence counsel in a criminal trial
senses.definitionCN: 刑事审判中与辩方律师相对的功能性角色
senses.example: The prosecutor and defence counsel agreed on the schedule of witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官与辩方律师就证人顺序达成一致。
senses.why: A trial is built as a contest of two offices, and naming one side by its task is the clearest way to mark the other.
senses.whyCN: 审判被搭成两个职位的较量，用任务来命名其中一方，是标记另一方最清楚的办法。

intro.en: Prosecutor is the agent noun of Latin prosequi 'to follow forward', with the agent suffix -or. Latin already had prosecutor for one who pursues, and English narrowed it to the officer who pursues a criminal charge.
intro.cn: prosecutor 是拉丁 prosequi「向前追随」的施事名词，带施事后缀 -or。拉丁语本就有 prosecutor 指「追逐者」，英语把它收窄为追究刑事指控的官员。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it also stands behind sequence and consecutive. In prosequi it supplies the idea of trailing after something until it is reached.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，也是 sequence 与 consecutive 的来源。在 prosequi 中，它提供「一直尾随直到抵达」的观念。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, to follow forward, to pursue, to continue. Legal usage applied it to the pursuit of a charge.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。法律用法把它用于对指控的追究。

items.en: Latin prosecutor named one who pursues or accompanies, a general agent noun with no special legal rank.
items.cn: 拉丁 prosecutor 指追逐者或随行者，是一般性的施事名词，没有专门的法律级别。

items.en: French legal writing used the corresponding agent noun for the officer conducting a case, and English took the pattern with the rest of its court vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语法律文书用相应的施事名词指推进案件的官员，英语连同其他法庭词汇一起接受了这个模式。

items.en: English prosecutor first meant any pursuer or executor, then settled on the officer who brings the state's criminal case.
items.cn: 英语的 prosecutor 最初指任何追逐者或执行者，后来固定为提起国家刑事案件的官员。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for the courtroom lawyer, for the office that screens charges, and for titled posts such as federal prosecutor.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指庭上的公诉律师、负责筛查指控的机关，以及联邦检察官这类带名号的职位。

note.en: Group one separates the related nouns and verb from a hostile-prefix look-alike and from a mineral-seeker that only sounds similar; group two lists the titles used for the same office in different systems.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根名词与动词、一个带敌对前缀的形近词，以及一个只是读音相近的「找矿者」；第二组列出不同体系对同一职位的称呼。

entries.definition: The proceeding or the team; the prosecutor is the individual lawyer who conducts it.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序或团队；prosecutor 是推进程序的那位律师。

entries.definition: To bring and conduct the case; the prosecutor is the person doing it.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起并推进案件；prosecutor 是做这件事的人。

entries.definition: One who persecutes or harasses, from per- 'through'; the prefix turns following into mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指迫害者、骚扰者，来自 per-「贯穿」；前缀把「跟随」变成「迫害」。

entries.definition: One who searches for minerals, from prospicere 'to look forward'; it looks and sounds close but has no following verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指找矿者，来自 prospicere「向前看」；外形与读音都接近，却没有「跟随」这个动词。

entries.definition: Relating to the office or its practices, not a person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指与该职位或其做法有关的，不是担任者本人。

entries.definition: The elected official who prosecutes cases in a county or district.
entries.definitionCN: 在郡或地区负责起诉的民选官员。

entries.definition: The official who conducts prosecutions for a state or county, a regional variant of the same role.
entries.definitionCN: 为州或郡进行起诉的官员，是同一角色的地区变体。

entries.definition: The prosecutor acting for the Crown in Commonwealth systems.
entries.definitionCN: 在英联邦体系中代表王室起诉的检察官。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for the lawyer appearing for the public; prosecutor is the established title.
entries.definitionCN: 对代表公众出庭的律师的描述性说法；prosecutor 是既定称谓。

entries.definition: The collective client on whose behalf the prosecutor acts, not the lawyer.
entries.definitionCN: 指检察官所代表的集体委托人，不是律师本人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real following verb and the real differences between pursuing, harassing and looking forward.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「跟随」动词，以及「追究」「迫害」「向前看」三者之间的真实差别。

normal.en: The prosecutor follows the charge forward; that is what the verb means.
normal.cn: 检察官把指控向前追；这正是那个动词的意思。

normal.en: Persecutor shares the following verb but adds a prefix of 'through': harassment, not litigation.
normal.cn: persecutor 共享「跟随」动词，却加了「贯穿」前缀：那是迫害，不是诉讼。

normal.en: Prospector comes from looking forward, not from following: a miner, not a lawyer.
normal.cn: prospector 来自「向前看」，不是「跟随」：那是找矿人，不是律师。

normal.en: Fixed phrases name the office: public prosecutor, federal prosecutor, the prosecutor's office.
normal.cn: 固定说法点明职位：公诉人、联邦检察官、检察官办公室。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer standing behind a row of numbered evidence bags, a national emblem on the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一位律师站在一排编号证据袋后，墙上挂着国徽。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that most accusations never pass through, kept by one official with a file in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门，多数指控都过不去，守门者手里拿着一份卷宗。

abstract.en: Picture two seats facing each other, one marked with the public's name, one with a private client's.
abstract.cn: 想象两把相对的椅子，一把写着公众的名字，一把写着私人委托人的名字。

examples.en: The prosecutor must share all exculpatory evidence with the defence.
examples.cn: 检察官必须向辩方披露全部有利于被告的证据。

examples.en: A prosecutor decides whether a file goes forward, not whether the person is guilty.
examples.cn: 检察官决定一份卷宗是否继续推进，而不是决定那个人是否有罪。

examples.en: The prosecutor and the defence lawyer argued over the admissibility of the recording.
examples.cn: 检察官与辩护律师就录音能否采纳展开争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究特」——把诉状一层层剖开、追到底的那个特别角色 → 检察官

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的施事名词 prosecutor，由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成，词尾 -or 表施事者；英语收窄为「检察官」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the state's courtroom lawyer, through the gatekeeping official, the presenter of evidence, the ranked post, the old pursuer, the voice of the public, the loose accuser, and the opposing role at trial.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从庭上的国家律师开始，经把关官员、证据出示者、有级别的职位、旧时的追行者、公众的代言人、泛称的指控者，最后到审判中的对抗角色。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lawyer behind numbered evidence bags, an emblem on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位律师站在编号证据袋后，墙上挂着徽记。

branches.en: THE LAWYER: the agent of the charge, the one who follows it through court.
branches.cn: 律师：指控的执行者，把它一路追过法庭的人。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: screening files and holding a rank are the same post seen from inside the system.
branches.cn: 职位：筛查卷宗与占据级别，是同一职位在体系内部的两种看法。

branches.en: THE VOICE: presenting proof in court and pressing an accusation outside it both mean speaking for a charge.
branches.cn: 声音：在庭上出示证据、在庭外推动指控，都是替一项指控发声。

branches.en: THE OLD SENSE: before criminal law claimed the word, a prosecutor was simply one who carried a task through.
branches.cn: 旧义：刑法接管这个词之前，检察官只是把一项任务执行到底的人。

branches.en: THE COUNTERPART: the office speaks for the public and therefore stands opposite the defence.
branches.cn: 对应面：这个职位替公众发声，因此与辩方相对而立。

intro.en: Prosecutor is a Latin agent noun on a verb of following, and its ending is what makes it a person rather than a process.
intro.cn: prosecutor 是建立在「跟随」动词上的拉丁施事名词，词尾正是它成为人而非过程的原因。

latinIntro.en: The pieces are pro- 'forth', sequi 'follow' and -or 'one who'; Latin already formed prosecutor from them, and English kept the shape.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是 pro-「向前」、sequi「跟随」与 -or「做某事的人」；拉丁语已用它们构成 prosecutor，英语保留了这一形态。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀给跟随指定方向）
items.example: The prefix points the following forward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把跟随指向前方。

items.meaningCN: 跟随
向前追随；追究
执行动作的人（施事后缀把动作转成施事者）
items.example: Doctor and victor share the ending.
items.exampleCN: doctor 与 victor 共享这个词尾。

items.meaningCN: 追究指控的人（由过程转为职责承担者）
对指控的追究（名词后缀把动作转成程序）

items.meaning: to bring and conduct a case
items.meaningCN: 提起并推进案件（回到动作本身）
与该职位有关的（形容词后缀把角色转成属性）

definition_zh: 起诉；检控；（正式）继续从事、推行；追究到底
definition_en: to bring a criminal charge against someone and conduct the case
core_image: 一个人把一份文件按在桌上，沿着页边的编号一页页往下翻，翻到最后一页才停手
scene: 检方拿到新的银行记录之后，决定对那名会计正式提出指控。The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 prosecute 指对某人正式提起刑事指控并推进案件（第 1 个义项：提起刑事起诉）；句意：新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。图中可辨识物件：银行记录、案卷页码、检察官办公桌、印章。

pos.zh: 起诉；检控（对某人提起并推进刑事指控）
提起公诉；进行起诉
（正式）继续从事、推行（某项工作、调查或事业）

collocations.zh: 进行战争（旧式正式说法）

senses.title: Bring a criminal charge
senses.definition: to formally charge someone with an offence
senses.definitionCN: 正式指控某人犯罪
senses.example: The state chose to prosecute the accountant after the new bank records arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 新的银行记录到手后，州一方决定起诉那名会计。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind prosecution: what the office does when it decides a file should go to court.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 prosecution 背后的动作：当机构认定一份卷宗该送进法院时，它做的就是这件事。

senses.title: Conduct the case in court
senses.definition: to present and argue the state's case through the hearings
senses.definitionCN: 在庭审中陈述并论证国家的案件
senses.example: The office prosecuted the case for nearly two years.
senses.exampleCN: 该机关把这桩案子推进了近两年。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to follow forward, so the work is a long following of the case rather than a single filing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为向前追随，所以这项工作是对案件的长程追随，而非一次立案。

senses.title: Press a civil claim
senses.definition: in legal writing, to pursue a claim or a suit to judgment
senses.definitionCN: 在法律文字中，把请求或诉讼追究至判决
senses.example: The creditor prosecuted the debt through two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 债权人通过两级法院追究这笔债务。
senses.why: Before criminal law dominated the word, any claim could be prosecuted, and older legal writing still uses it that way.
senses.whyCN: 在刑法主导这个词之前，任何请求都可以被「追究」，较早的法律文字仍这样使用。

senses.title: Carry on an activity
senses.definition: in formal style, to continue or carry on a study, inquiry or policy
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，继续或推行一项研究、调查或政策
senses.example: The committee prosecuted its inquiry despite the delays.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管一再拖延，委员会仍把调查进行下去。
senses.why: The oldest sense is continuation, and formal prose keeps it alive for any sustained effort, not only for lawsuits.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是「继续」，正式文字把它保留下来，用于任何持续的努力，而不限于诉讼。

senses.title: Pursue a war or campaign
senses.definition: in older usage, to carry a war or campaign forward energetically
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，有力地推进战争或战役
senses.example: The general prosecuted the campaign into the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 将军把战役推进到了冬季。
senses.why: Military writing used the verb for pressing an operation to its end, and that usage survives in histories and formal reports.
senses.whyCN: 军事文字用这个动词表示把一次行动压到终点，这一用法保存在史书与正式报告里。

senses.title: Carry out a duty or plan
senses.definition: in formal style, to carry out a duty, plan or design
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文体中，执行一项职责、计划或设计
senses.example: She prosecuted the plan with a patience few colleagues shared.
senses.exampleCN: 她以少有人能及的耐心把这项计划执行下去。
senses.why: Any design can be followed through, and formal English uses the verb for that steady execution without any legal charge.
senses.whyCN: 任何设计都可以被贯彻到底，正式英语便用这个动词表示那种稳定的执行，与刑事指控无关。

senses.title: Follow up an appeal or remedy
senses.definition: to carry a legal remedy forward to the next stage
senses.definitionCN: 把一项法律救济推进到下一阶段
senses.example: They prosecuted the appeal all the way to the higher court.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把上诉一路推进到高等法院。
senses.why: A remedy has stages, and the verb marks the act of not letting the matter drop at the first refusal.
senses.whyCN: 救济是有阶段的，这个动词标记的正是「第一次被驳回也不放手」的那个动作。

senses.title: Pursue a goal relentlessly
senses.definition: in literary style, to pursue an aim with persistence
senses.definitionCN: 在文学文体中，坚持不懈地追求一个目标
senses.example: He prosecuted his ambition long after his friends had given up theirs.
senses.exampleCN: 朋友们早已放弃各自的抱负，他仍把自己的追求推进下去。
senses.why: The core image of following forward can describe any long pursuit, which is why the verb appears in writing about ambition.
senses.whyCN: 「向前追随」的核心意象可以描述任何长程追求，所以这个动词会出现在写抱负的文字里。

intro.en: Prosecute comes from the stem of Latin prosecutus, the past participle of prosequi 'to follow forward'. The verb was formed in English from that stem, and its oldest sense is continuation.
intro.cn: prosecute 来自拉丁 prosecutus 的词干，那是 prosequi「向前追随」的过去分词。这个动词是在英语中用该词干构成的，最古老的含义是「继续」。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it also stands behind sequence and consecutive, so the idea of one thing after another runs through the whole family.
items.cn: sequi 意为跟随，也是 sequence 与 consecutive 的来源，所以「一件接一件」的观念贯穿整族词。

items.en: Pro- 'forth' plus sequi gave prosequi, 'to follow forward, pursue, continue'. Roman legal writing used it for pursuing a charge.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 sequi 构成 prosequi，意为向前追随、追求、继续。罗马法律文字用它表示追究一项指控。

items.en: The past participle prosecutus supplied the stem prosecut-, which English took as the base of both the verb and the nouns.
items.cn: 过去分词 prosecutus 提供词干 prosecut-，英语以它作为动词与名词的共同基础。

items.en: English formed prosecute from the participle stem, at first for continuing any business, then increasingly for the pursuit of a legal case.
items.cn: 英语用这个分词词干构成 prosecute，起初指继续任何事务，后来越来越多指追究一桩法律案件。

items.en: Legal writing fixed the criminal sense, pairing prosecute with indictment and trial, while the older sense of continuing survived in formal prose.
items.cn: 法律文字固定了刑事义，把 prosecute 与起诉、审判配对使用；而「继续」的旧义保存在正式散文中。

items.en: Modern English uses the verb mainly for criminal charges, with the sense of carrying out a duty, inquiry or war kept for formal and historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用这个动词指刑事指控；执行职责、进行调查或进行战争的义项则留给正式与历史文字。

note.en: Group one separates the related nouns from the classic hostile-prefix confusion and from a look-alike about looking forward; group two sets the verb against the other verbs of charging and suing.
note.cn: 第一组区分同根名词、经典的「敌对前缀」混淆词，以及一个关于「向前看」的形近词；第二组把这个动词与其他表示指控和起诉的动词作对照。

entries.definition: To harass or oppress, from per- 'through' plus the same following verb; the prefix replaces pursuit with mistreatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指骚扰、压迫，由 per-「贯穿」加同一个「跟随」动词构成；前缀把「追究」换成「迫害」。
