entries.definition: The proceeding or the team; the verb names the act, not the institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指程序或团队；动词命名的是动作，不是机构。

entries.definition: The lawyer who performs the act; the verb does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 执行这个动作的律师；动词本身不指人。

entries.definition: An outlook or a search for minerals, from prospicere 'to look forward'; it shares no following verb with prosecute.
entries.definitionCN: 指前景或找矿，来自 prospicere「向前看」；它与 prosecute 不共享「跟随」动词。

entries.definition: Capable of being prosecuted, a quality of a case rather than an act.
entries.definitionCN: 指可被起诉的，是案件的性质，不是动作。

entries.definition: To charge formally, often after a grand jury; prosecute also covers the whole conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式起诉，常在大陪审团之后；prosecute 还覆盖案件的整个推进过程。

entries.definition: To state that someone has committed an offence; prosecute adds the decision and the conduct of the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指声明某人犯罪；prosecute 多了「决定起诉」与「推进案件」的意思。

entries.definition: To start a civil case; prosecute is the usual verb for criminal proceedings and can also mean carrying any claim forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指提起民事诉讼；prosecute 常用于刑事程序，也可指把任何请求推进下去。

entries.definition: To hear and decide a case in court; prosecute is the state's part before and during that hearing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法庭上审理并裁决；prosecute 是国家在庭审前后所做的那一部分。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for following an aim or a person; prosecute is its formal and legal doublet.
entries.definitionCN: 指追求目标或追踪某人的日常动词；prosecute 是它在正式与法律语境中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real participle stem and the real contrast between following a charge and harassing a person.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的分词词干，以及「追究指控」与「迫害他人」之间的真实对比。

normal.en: Prosequi is to follow forward: prosecuting a case means not letting it drop.
normal.cn: prosequi 是向前追：起诉一桩案子就是不让它掉在地上。

normal.en: Persecute has the same following verb but a prefix of 'through': it follows a person to hurt, not to court.
normal.cn: persecute 共享「跟随」动词，但前缀是「贯穿」：它跟住一个人是为了伤害，不是为了上法院。

normal.en: Prospect is about looking forward, not following: a different verb entirely.
normal.cn: prospect 讲的是向前看，不是跟随：完全另一个动词。

normal.en: The family runs prosecute, prosecution, prosecutor and prosecutorial.
normal.cn: 同族词有 prosecute、prosecution、prosecutor、prosecutorial。

normal.en: The old sense still works: a committee can prosecute an inquiry without charging anyone.
normal.cn: 旧义仍然可用：委员会可以把一项调查进行下去，而不指控任何人。

abstract.en: Picture a finger walking down a numbered page, page after page, until the last one.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指沿着编号的页面往下走，一页又一页，直到最后一页。

abstract.en: Picture a charge as a heavy door that must be pushed open again at every stage.
abstract.cn: 想象指控是一扇沉重的门，每到一个阶段都得再推一次。

abstract.en: Picture a person who keeps pursuing a goal after everyone else has stopped.
abstract.cn: 想象别人都停下之后，仍有一个人在追求那个目标。

examples.en: The state may prosecute only if the evidence meets a fixed standard.
examples.cn: 只有证据达到固定标准，州一方才可以起诉。

examples.en: They prosecuted him for fraud and lost the first hearing.
examples.cn: 他们以欺诈罪起诉他，却输掉了第一次庭审。

examples.en: The council prosecuted the inquiry for three years.
examples.cn: 委员会把这项调查进行了三年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「剖诉究」——把诉状剖开、一路追到底 → 起诉、检控

root: 拉丁 prosequi（向前追随、追究）的过去分词 prosecutus 的词干 prosecut-；由 pro-（向前）加 sequi（跟随）构成。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from bringing a criminal charge, through conducting the case, pursuing a civil claim, carrying on an inquiry, pressing a war, executing a plan, following up an appeal, and pursuing a goal in literary style.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从提起刑事指控开始，经推进案件、追究民事请求、进行调查、推进战争、执行计划、追究上诉，最后到文学文体中的执着追求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger walking down a numbered page to the last line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着编号的页面走到最后一行。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: the act starts a criminal case and then keeps it moving.
branches.cn: 指控：这个动作启动刑事案件，然后又不断把它往前推。

branches.en: THE CIVIL CLAIM: the same verb reaches claims that are not criminal at all.
branches.cn: 民事请求：同一个动词也覆盖完全不属于刑事的请求。

branches.en: THE FORMAL EFFORT: any inquiry, duty or plan can be carried forward.
branches.cn: 正式的努力：任何调查、职责或计划都可以被推行。

branches.en: THE CAMPAIGN: wars and appeals are both pressed on to their next stage.
branches.cn: 推进：战争与上诉都被压向下一阶段。

branches.en: THE LITERARY EDGE: the same following motion becomes a picture of relentless ambition.
branches.cn: 文学边缘：同一个「追随」动作成了不知停歇的抱负图景。

intro.en: Prosecute is a verb built on a Latin participle stem, and its endings are what turn that stem into an English action word.
intro.cn: prosecute 是建立在拉丁分词词干上的动词，词尾把那个词干变成英语的动作词。

latinIntro.en: Pro- 'forth', sequi 'follow' and the participle stem prosecut- are the pieces; English added the verb ending -e to make prosecute.
latinIntro.cn: 构件是 pro-「向前」、sequi「跟随」与分词词干 prosecut-；英语加上动词词尾 -e 构成 prosecute。

items.meaningCN: 向前、向外（前缀把跟随指向前方）
跟随
向前追随；追究
已追究的（提供英语词干 prosecut-）
追究一项指控（由词干加动词词尾，成为可变化的英语动词）
对案件的追究（名词后缀把动作转成程序）
追究指控的人（施事后缀把动作转成施事者）
可被起诉的（形容词后缀把动作转成可能性）

definition_zh: 指控；指责；控告；（正式的）罪状
definition_en: a statement or charge that someone has done something wrong
core_image: 一个人伸出手指指向对面，桌上摊着一份写满日期的纸，被指的人低头看着自己的手
scene: 会议结束前，有人把一份错账清单推到桌子中间，点名说是某位同事改的。The accusation named a colleague and gave a date for every altered entry.
sceneCN: 这里 accusation 指对某人做了错事的指控（第 1 个义项：指出他人有错的指控）；句意：这项指控点名了一位同事，并为每一笔被改动的账目给出日期。图中可辨识物件：错账清单、手指、会议桌、日期栏。

pos.zh: 指控；指责（指出某人做了错事）
（法律）控告；罪状

senses.title: A charge that someone did wrong
senses.definition: a statement asserting that a person has done something wrong
senses.definitionCN: 断言某人做了错事的话
senses.example: The accusation named a colleague and gave a date for every altered entry.
senses.exampleCN: 这项指控点名了一位同事，并为每一笔被改动的账目给出日期。
senses.why: The noun is the content of the act of accusing, so it can be written down, read aloud and answered point by point.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词是「指控」这一动作的内容，所以它可以被写下、被宣读，也可以被逐条回应。

senses.title: The act of accusing
senses.definition: the act of saying that someone is at fault
senses.definitionCN: 说某人有过错的这个动作
senses.example: His accusation came after months of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 他沉默数月之后才作出指控。
senses.why: Like many action nouns, it can name either the words spoken or the speaking of them, which is why it takes no article in some phrases.
senses.whyCN: 和许多动作名词一样，它既可指说出口的话，也可指说出这些话的动作，所以在一些说法里不带冠词。

senses.title: A formal legal charge
senses.definition: a formal charge of wrongdoing brought in legal proceedings
senses.definitionCN: 在法律程序中提出的正式罪状
senses.example: The accusation was read out before the magistrate.
senses.exampleCN: 这项控告在治安法官面前被宣读。
senses.why: Law borrows the everyday word for blame and stiffens it into a charge that must be answered on the record.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用日常的「责备」一词，把它硬化成一项必须在案卷上作答的罪状。

senses.title: An unproven allegation
senses.definition: a claim of wrongdoing that has not yet been proved
senses.definitionCN: 尚未被证明的犯错主张
senses.example: The accusation collapsed once the timestamps were checked.
senses.exampleCN: 时间戳一核对，这项指称就站不住了。
senses.why: The word asserts rather than proves, so it naturally covers claims still waiting for evidence, which is why it often carries a cautious tone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是「断言」而非「证明」，所以天然覆盖仍在等证据的主张，也因此常带谨慎语气。

senses.title: Blame or recrimination
senses.definition: blame exchanged between people, often in a quarrel
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间交换的责备，常出现在争吵中
senses.example: The meeting ended in mutual accusations about missed deadlines.
senses.exampleCN: 会议在互相指责错过的截止日期中结束。
senses.why: When blame travels in both directions, the plural noun describes the exchange rather than any single charge.
senses.whyCN: 当责备朝两个方向来回时，复数形式描述的是这场交换，而不是任何一项单独的指控。

senses.title: The charge as a written statement
senses.definition: the document or statement in which a charge is set out
senses.definitionCN: 列明指控的文书或陈述
senses.example: A copy of the accusation was handed to the accused.
senses.exampleCN: 一份罪状副本被交给了被告。
senses.why: Once a charge is recorded, the paper itself can be called by the name of what it contains, a common shift from words to document.
senses.whyCN: 指控一旦被记录，那张纸本身就可以用它承载的内容来称呼，这是从「话语」到「文书」的常见转移。

senses.title: A criticism of a practice or quality
senses.titleCN: 对某种做法或品质的批评
senses.definition: a public criticism aimed at a practice, policy or quality rather than a person
senses.definitionCN: 针对做法、政策或品质而非个人的公开批评
senses.example: The report rejected accusations of waste in the building programme.
senses.exampleCN: 报告驳回了对建设计划铺张浪费的指责。
senses.why: Public argument often targets a habit or a system, and the word extends from people to practices without losing its accusing force.
senses.whyCN: 公共争论常把矛头指向某种习气或制度，这个词便从人扩展到做法，而指责的力道不减。

senses.title: The formal statement of a charge in old law
senses.definition: in older legal usage, the formal declaration of a criminal charge
senses.definitionCN: 在较早法律用法中，对刑事指控的正式声明
senses.example: The roll records the accusation and the day it was sworn.
senses.exampleCN: 卷册记下了控状以及宣誓的那一天。
senses.why: Older procedure had a distinct step of formally declaring the charge, and legal histories still use the noun for that document.
senses.whyCN: 较早的程序有一个单独步骤，专门正式宣告指控，法律史著作仍用这个名词指那份文书。

intro.en: Accusation comes from Latin accusatio, the noun of accusare 'to call to account, to charge'. The verb is ad- 'to' plus causa 'cause, legal case'. The deeper origin of causa is source uncertain; it also stands behind cause, excuse and recuse.
intro.cn: accusation 来自拉丁 accusatio，即 accusare「传唤问责、指控」的名词。这个动词是 ad-「向」加 causa「原因、法律案件」。causa 的更深来源属来源不确定；它也是 cause、excuse、recuse 的来源。

items.en: Causa meant a cause, a reason and a legal case. Its deeper origin is source uncertain, and the forms sometimes proposed for it are reconstructions rather than settled derivations.
items.cn: causa 指原因、理由与法律案件。其更深来源属来源不确定，偶尔为它提出的形式只是重构，并非已定的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus causa gave accusare, to bring a person to the case, hence to call to account, to charge. The image is a summons to answer in a cause.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 causa 构成 accusare，把一个人带到案件面前，因而意为问责、指控。意象是传唤其到某个案由中作答。

items.en: The noun accusatio named both the act of charging and the charge itself, a double value that English keeps in accusation.
items.cn: 名词 accusatio 既指指控这一动作，也指指控本身，这一双重价值被英语的 accusation 保留下来。

items.en: French legal writing carried the noun into court procedure, and English borrowed it with the rest of its Norman legal vocabulary.
items.cn: 法语法律文书把这个名词带入法庭程序，英语连同其他诺曼法律词汇一起借入。

items.en: English used accusation for formal charges and for ordinary blame, a range that later widened further into public criticism.
items.cn: 英语的 accusation 既用于正式控告，也用于日常责备，这一范围后来又扩展到公开批评。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for any claim of wrongdoing, from a courtroom charge to an argument about a policy, and the plurality of contexts keeps its accusing edge.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个词指任何「有人做错事」的主张，从法庭控告到针对政策的争论，多种语境都保留了它的指责锋芒。

note.en: Group one separates the verb and the derived adjectives from two words that share the same Latin case noun but take different prefixes, and from a grammatical term built on the same verb; group two sets the claim against the other names for a charge.
note.cn: 第一组区分动词与派生形容词、两个共享同一个拉丁「案由」名词但前缀不同的词，以及一个同出该动词的语法术语；第二组把这桩主张与其他指控名目作对照。

entries.definition: The act of charging someone; accusation is the charge or the charging, not the doing of it in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 指控某人的动作；accusation 是指控内容或指控这件事，而不是句中那个动作。

entries.definition: Carrying or expressing a charge; it describes a tone, not the charge itself.
entries.definitionCN: 带有或表达指控的；描述语气，而不是指控本身。

entries.tag: same Latin case noun, different prefix
entries.definition: To release from blame, from ex- 'out of' plus causa; it shares the case noun but reverses the direction of accusation.
entries.definitionCN: 指免除责任，由 ex-「出于」加 causa 构成；共享「案由」名词，方向却与指控相反。

entries.tag: same Latin case noun, different prefix
entries.definition: To withdraw from a case because of a conflict, from re- plus causa 'to refuse on a ground'; it is about stepping out, not charging.
entries.definitionCN: 指因利益冲突退出案件，由 re- 加 causa「以某理由拒绝」构成；它是退出，不是指控。

entries.definition: The grammatical case of the object, named through a translation of a Greek term for what is caused or affected; it has nothing to do with blaming.
entries.definitionCN: 指宾格，其命名经希腊语「受作用者」的译法而来；与责备无关。

entries.definition: A claim of wrongdoing made without proof, the cautious word in journalism; accusation is stronger and more personal.
entries.definitionCN: 指未经证明的犯错主张，是新闻中的谨慎用词；accusation 语气更强，也更针对个人。

entries.definition: A formal accusation, especially in law; it is the technical term that accusation approaches in legal settings.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式指控，尤用于法律；在法律场景中，accusation 接近这个技术术语。

entries.definition: A statement that something is wrong, often about a service; it may not name a person at fault.
entries.definitionCN: 指说明某事有问题的陈述，常针对服务；它不一定指名某人有过错。

entries.definition: The formal written charge in criminal procedure; accusation is the wider everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 指刑事程序中的正式书面起诉书；accusation 是范围更宽的日常词。

entries.definition: The assigning of responsibility for something bad; accusation is the statement of fault, blame is the weight placed on someone.
entries.definitionCN: 指把坏事的责任归给某人；accusation 是过错的主张，blame 是压在某人身上的重量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin case noun, the real prefix contrasts and the real legal pair.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「案由」名词、真实的前缀对比，以及真实的法律配对。

normal.en: Accusare is to bring someone to a case: ad- 'to' plus causa 'case'.
normal.cn: accusare 是把人带到案件面前：ad-「向」加 causa「案件」。

normal.en: Excuse and recuse share the case noun but move the other way: one takes a person out of blame, one takes a judge out of a case.
normal.cn: excuse 与 recuse 共享「案件」名词却朝相反方向：一个把人从责备中移出，一个把法官从案件中移出。

normal.en: Accusative is a grammar term from the same verb, not a word about blame.
normal.cn: accusative 是同一个动词衍生的语法术语，不是讲责备的词。

normal.en: Allegation is the cautious cousin: an accusation asserts, an allegation merely states.
normal.cn: allegation 是谨慎的表亲：accusation 作出断言，allegation 只是陈述。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the moves: make an accusation, deny an accusation, level an accusation against someone.
normal.cn: 固定说法展示动作：提出指控、否认指控、对某人提出指控。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pointed across a table at a sheet covered in dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指隔着桌子，指向一张写满日期的纸。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that must be answered before the room will move on.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话，必须在房间继续之前得到回答。

abstract.en: Picture blame as a weight that can be placed on a person and then lifted by evidence.
abstract.cn: 想象责备是一件可以压在某人身上的重物，也能被证据抬起。

examples.en: She answered the accusation with a single dated receipt.
examples.cn: 她用一张有日期的收据回应了这项指控。

examples.en: The accusation was never proved, though it damaged his career.
examples.cn: 这项指控从未被证实，却毁了他的事业。

examples.en: Public accusations of waste forced the department to publish its accounts.
examples.cn: 公众对铺张的指责迫使该部门公开账目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额求神」——有人额头上写着问号，指着你说「就是你」→ 指控、指责

root: 拉丁 accusare（问责、指控）的名词 accusatio，由 ad-（向）加 causa（原因、法律案件）构成；causa 更深来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a charge of wrongdoing, through the act of accusing, the formal legal charge, the unproven allegation, mutual blame, the written statement, public criticism of a practice, and the old formal declaration of a charge.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「某人做错事」的指控开始，经指控这一动作、正式法律控告、未经证实的指称、相互责备、书面罪状、对做法的公开批评，最后到旧法中的正式控状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pointed across a table at a dated sheet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指隔着桌子，指向一张写满日期的纸。

branches.en: THE WORDS: the same noun names both the charge and the act of saying it.
branches.cn: 话语：同一个名词既指指控内容，也指说出它的动作。

branches.en: THE LAW: formal procedure turns blame into a recorded charge that must be answered on the record.
branches.cn: 法律：正式程序把责备变成有记录的罪状，必须在案卷上作答。

branches.en: THE UNPROVEN: assert first, prove later, which is why the word can sound cautious.
branches.cn: 未证：先断言、后证明，所以这个词可能听起来谨慎。

branches.en: THE EXCHANGE: in a quarrel blame travels both ways and the plural noun describes the traffic.
branches.cn: 交换：争吵中责备来回流动，复数形式描述的正是这股来回。

branches.en: THE PAPER AND THE PUBLIC: a charge can become a document, and its target can be a practice rather than a person.
branches.cn: 文书与公众：指控可以成为一份文书，其对象也可以是一种做法而非某个人。

intro.en: Accusation is a Latin action noun whose base is a compound of a prefix and a noun, so its parts explain why a charge is 'brought to a case'.
intro.cn: accusation 是拉丁动作名词，其基础是前缀与名词的复合，构件正解释了为什么指控是「把人带到案件面前」。

latinIntro.en: Ad- 'to' plus causa 'cause, legal case' gives accusare; the participle accusatus and the noun accusatio supply the stem, and -tion makes the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: ad-「向」加 causa「原因、法律案件」构成 accusare；分词 accusatus 与名词 accusatio 提供词干，-tion 构成英语名词。

items.meaningCN: 向、朝（前缀把动作指向某人与某案）
items.example: The prefix points the charge at a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把指控指向某个人。

items.meaningCN: 原因；理由；法律案件
items.example: The noun named the case itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词命名案件本身。

items.meaningCN: 问责；指控（把人带到案由前要求作答）
已被指控的（分词提供英语词干 accusat-）
动作或其结果（名词后缀把动词转成事体）
items.example: The suffix made a noun of the charge.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把指控变成名词。

items.meaningCN: 对过错的指控（动作与内容共用一词）
指控某人（去掉名词词尾，回到动作）
items.example: They accuse the company of waste.

items.meaningCN: 用于……的、带有……性质的（形容词后缀把动作转成属性）
items.exampleCN: 指责性的话结束了会议。

items.meaning: the grammatical case of the object
items.meaningCN: 宾格（语法术语，同出该动词但语义另行发展）
items.example: The noun is in the accusative.
